Evidence: crates/eve-server/src/services/fleet_social_fleet_ops.rs:882; test: test_so_fleets_..._disband (tests/it/social_fleets_complete.rs:911, ~L1032) — asserts shield/armor ratios in the return and that an OnFleetStateChange was emitted; test_so2_fleet_manager_hierarchy_broadcast_and_fleet_warp (social_fleets_corps.rs:572); live: client_notifications.json OnFleetStateChange consumers; fleetWatchList.pyj; knowledge Expected behaviour: AddToWatchlist(memberCharID) for a member of the caller's fleet registers that member. Afterwards, whenever the member's ship takes damage, the caller receives periodic damage-state updates (shield/armor/hull ratios) until RemoveFromWatchlist or one of them leaves the fleet. A non-member target is rejected.

Aliased to AddToWatchlist. arg0 is the client's list of favorites, but as_i64() fails on a List, so target_id defaults to the caller's own char_id: the caller watches itself and the passed members are ignored. One-shot notification, and the set has no consumer. Evidence: crates/eve-server/src/services/fleet_social_fleet_ops.rs:882; test: test_so_fleets_..._disband (tests/it/social_fleets_complete.rs:911, ~L1036) — calls with [List[charID]] and only checks it doesn't error; live: client:eve/client/script/parklife/fleetSvc.pyj; knowledge Expected behaviour: RegisterForDamageUpdates([charA, charB]) replaces the caller's registered set with those fleet members. Damage to any of them then streams damage-state updates (charID, shield, armor, hull ratios) to the caller; members not in the list produce none. Passing an empty list stops all updates.

Because no damage updates are ever streamed (see AddToWatchlist), removal has no observable effect. Returns a KeyVal with fake ratios. Untested beyond not erroring. Combined with the OnFleetMove that MoveMember sends, a real client calling FinishMove() after each move would be demoted. (Live arg list inferred; Crucible has only the OnFleetMove side.) fw_system_occupations is never populated in production (only tests insert it), so the fallback always runs. It treats every low-sec system (0<sec<0.45) as a warzone, with owner/occupier = first station's owner faction or Caldari. Field names (ownerFactionID/occupierFactionID/frontlineStatus) may not match the client's occupationState attributes (e.g. occupierID/adjacencyState). rows.acceptance: An insurgency spawns around a low-sec FW frontline system with 4 starting systems; a 48h Forecasting phase announces FOB location and systems, spawns no insurgency sites and keeps the FOB invulnerable; the Active phase lasts at most 7 days; a 48h wind-down follows. insurgencySolarsystem.GetAllVisibleCampaigns/GetLocalCampaignClientSnapshot report the current phase and timers.
rows.title: Insurgency phases (forecast / active / wind-down)
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.insurgency only covers corruption/suppression read-out and feat:fw.fw-pirate is a single line; the phase machine, with its V24.01 timings (48h forecast, 7-day max), has no testable row.

rows.acceptance: The pirate FOB spawns in the insurgency hub system and is dockable only by the pirate militia. It becomes attackable only once the Empire side reaches its suppression goal, and uses a single 3h (±1h jitter) armor reinforcement timer. Destroying it raises Suppression by one level (max 5) in every affected system and ends the insurgency as an Empire win.
rows.title: Pirate Forward Operating Base
rows.why_missing: No ledger row mentions the FOB structure, its vulnerability gate or its reinforcement timer; pirate-strongholds is a different Quasar package.

rows.acceptance: Win target = 5 fully suppressed/corrupted systems + the side's Ambition modifier (0..+5, only one side positive). A win adds +1 to the winner's modifier; an underdog win reduces the leader's modifier by 1. A pirate win gives temporary control of the FOB system, and that system's infrastructure hub becomes vulnerable 24h + 1 downtime after surrender. A side that misses its goal produces a tie with no bonus.
rows.title: Insurgency victory conditions and Ambition modifier
rows.why_missing: Victory resolution and the persistent ambition counter are absent from every fw/pve row.

rows.acceptance: When a system reaches Corruption level 3, an adjacent system with security 0.0–0.8 joins the insurgency and starts spawning sites. If no adjacent system is valid, a random valid system adjacent to the insurgency is chosen.
rows.title: Insurgency spread to adjacent systems
rows.why_missing: No row defines insurgency area growth; it was changed to level 3 in V24.01.

rows.acceptance: Each Corruption and Suppression stage (1–5) applies that stage's published system effects: security posture changes via securityMgr.get_modified_systems, plus the stage-gated site spawns and NPC behaviour. Effects are removed when the stage drops.
rows.title: Per-stage corruption/suppression system effects
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.insurgency only requires that levels are returned and change; feat:crimewatch.security-bands only reads modified systems. The stage→effect table is untested.

rows.acceptance: At insurgency end, contributors on the winning side are paid ISK+LP scaled by personal corruption/suppression contribution: maximum at 45% personal contribution, capped at 1,500,000 LP, with a 1.0x multiplier for winners and 0.4x for losers. Ties pay no bonus.
rows.title: Insurgency contribution payouts
rows.why_missing: No reward row exists for insurgency outcomes; fw-lp covers complexes/kills only.

rows.title: Insurgency Corporate Outpost Raid complexes
rows.why_missing: Insurgency site types are not listed anywhere in the ledger.

rows.acceptance: An ORE Rorqual NPC is tackled by pirate NPCs. Pirate militia complete the site when the ransom is paid; Empire militia complete it when the pirates are killed and the Rorqual warps off. The Rorqual can be destroyed and looted, which forfeits the LP but keeps the corruption. The LP payout is shared by up to 5 players.
rows.title: Insurgency Mining Op Ambush
rows.why_missing: Not covered by any pve/fw row.

rows.title: Ice Refinery Heist
rows.why_missing: The client calls a dedicated RPC for this content, but no feat row describes its gameplay.

rows.acceptance: At corruption/suppression thresholds, roaming named NPCs drop special loot. Pirates hand it in at Laundering Facilities in the FOB system; Empire militia hand it in at Counter-Insurgency Outposts in the War HQ systems (Mehatoor/Onnamon/Intaki/Amo). Each hand-in returns reward crates.
rows.title: Pirate Laundering Facilities / Counter-Insurgency Outposts
rows.why_missing: No row covers the item turn-in exchange or War HQ outposts.

rows.acceptance: FW battlefields spawn per warzone rules, with a 4h respawn persisted across downtime. Completing a battlefield objective pays 150,000 LP to the winning militia and applies its victory-point and advantage effect.
rows.title: FW battlefield site gameplay
rows.why_missing: feat:fw.fw-site-dungeons only requires listing battlefield instances; the site's gameplay, payout and respawn are not covered.

rows.acceptance: When a FW system reaches 100% contested (or after a pirate insurgency surrender), its infrastructure hub becomes vulnerable. Destroying it flips occupancy to the attacking militia and updates frontline/command/rearguard status. The hub regenerates if left alone.
rows.title: FW infrastructure hub capture
rows.why_missing: feat:fw.system-capture says 'becomes vulnerable' but does not specify the IHub structure that must be destroyed.

rows.acceptance: Incursions spawn in eligible constellations, with staging/vanguard/assault/HQ system roles assigned. After the mothership dies, the incursion withdraws on a timer and a new one spawns per cadence. map.GetSystemsInIncursions and GetIncursionGlobalReport reflect live state.
rows.title: Incursion spawn and withdrawal lifecycle
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.incursion-system packs constellations, influence, four site classes and payouts into one line, the same failure mode as the old single 'mining' row.

rows.acceptance: Influence starts at 100%. Each completed site reduces it by the site-class amount, and it regenerates over time while sites are not run. Low influence unlocks the mothership site.
rows.title: Incursion influence meter
rows.why_missing: Influence dynamics are hidden in feat:pve.incursion-system.

rows.acceptance: While an incursion is active, the constellation applies the Sansha system effects (resistance/damage penalties, bounty and LP reductions) via system-wide dbuffs. Their magnitude scales with influence, and they are removed on withdrawal.
rows.title: Incursion constellation effects
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.system-wide-effects lists wormholes/Pochven/storms but not incursions; no incursion row requires these effects.

rows.acceptance: corpRegistry.PayoutDividend pays ISK from a corp wallet division either per share to shareholders or equally to members. Both sides are journaled, and the call fails with insufficient funds or without the required role.
rows.title: Pay dividends
rows.why_missing: feat:corporation.corp-shares only says 'shares owned; votes weighted'. The client calls PayoutDividend and no row covers it.

rows.acceptance: MoveCompanyShares and MovePrivateShares transfer shares between the corporation and characters/corps. GetShareholders, GetSharesByShareholder and GetMemberIDsWithMoreThanAvgShares reflect the new distribution, which is then used for vote weighting.
rows.title: Share transfers
rows.why_missing: No row describes moving shares; corp-shares is coarse.

rows.acceptance: SetCorpWelcomeMail stores the template (role-gated) and GetCorpWelcomeMail returns it. The mail is delivered automatically to each new member on joining.
rows.title: Corporation welcome mail
rows.why_missing: Mailing-list welcome mail is covered, but the corp-level welcome mail RPCs have no feat row.

rows.acceptance: RegisterNewCorpMailRestrictionSettings toggles the restriction and DoesCorpRestrictCorpMails reports it. When it is on, only authorised role holders can send mail to the whole corporation; other members get the live UserError.
rows.title: Corp-wide mail restriction
rows.why_missing: feat:social.mail-corp-alliance does not include the restriction setting.

rows.acceptance: RegisterNewAcceptStructureSettings and DoesMyCorpAcceptStructures persist whether the corp accepts Upwell structure ownership transfers. Transfers to a corp that refuses them are rejected.
rows.title: Accept structure transfers setting
rows.why_missing: Not part of feat:corporation.corp-structure-ownership acceptance; the RPC pair has no behaviour row.

rows.acceptance: SetStructureReinforceDefault stores the corp default reinforce hour (role-gated) and GetStructureReinforceDefault returns it. Newly onlined corp structures adopt it.
rows.title: Corp default reinforcement hour
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.vulnerability-schedule covers only per-structure changes.

rows.acceptance: Kicks that cannot run immediately (for example, the member is in space or has pending role removals) are queued and executed when the live-server conditions are met. GetPendingAutoKicks lists them, and the queued member is removed and notified on execution.
rows.title: Deferred (auto) kicks
rows.why_missing: feat:corporation.kick-member only covers immediate kicks and CanBeKickedOut.

rows.acceptance: ResignFromCEO removes the CEO, and the corp enters a CEO-vacant state until a successor is chosen through the CEO vote case. GetNumberOfPotentialCEOs and voteManager.CanRunForCEO gate candidacy.
rows.title: CEO resignation
rows.why_missing: feat:corporation.ceo-change covers assignment and votes, but not the resignation path.

rows.acceptance: SetTakesFleetWarp, SetAcceptsRegroupValue and SetAcceptsConduitJumpsValue persist per member and appear in member info. Fleet warps, regroup actions and Pochven conduit group jumps skip members who have opted out.
rows.title: Fleet warp / regroup / conduit opt-ins
rows.why_missing: Three fleetObjectHandler RPCs change who is moved by fleet commands; fleet-warp-cmd ignores opt-outs and no row covers regroup or conduit opt-in.

rows.acceptance: fleetObjectHandler.LoadFleetSetup applies a saved setup atomically: wing/squad structure and names, MOTD, free-move/auto-join options and max size. It is boss-only, and members receive the change notifications.
rows.title: Load fleet setup
rows.why_missing: No row covers fleet setup loading.

rows.acceptance: MakeLeader transfers fleet boss to another member. When the boss leaves or disconnects, boss passes automatically per V24 rules, and all members are notified.
rows.title: Fleet boss hand-over
rows.why_missing: Boss transfer is not in roles-positions or leave-kick acceptance.

rows.acceptance: Ships colliding with other ships, structures or celestial hulls exchange momentum according to mass and velocity: no interpenetration, bumped ships are knocked off alignment and velocity, and the destiny updates are broadcast to observers. This is SDE-mass driven.
rows.title: Ball collisions (bumping)
rows.why_missing: No navigation row covers collision physics, although bumping is a core tactic (gate/structure bumping, anti-warp bumping).

rows.acceptance: Warping to a celestial lands at its warp-in point; warping to a station or stargate lands at its docking or jump perimeter. Warps to targets closer than 150 km are refused with the live error. The requested 0–100 km offset is applied relative to the landing point.
rows.title: Warp-in points and minimum warp distance
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.warp-to covers phases and distance only; landing geometry and the minimum distance are untested.

rows.acceptance: Supercarriers and titans are refused docking at NPC stations with the live UserError. Other capitals follow the V24 station docking rules.
rows.title: Supercapital NPC station docking refusal
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.dock-station covers only range and timers, and dock-structure only Upwell size rules.

rows.acceptance: Ships enter gated pockets by acceleration gate and land at the gate destination; warping directly into later gated rooms is impossible. MicroWarpdrive activation is refused in pockets whose dungeon or room data disallows it, and this is data-driven.
rows.title: Deadspace pocket restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.acceleration-gates covers only gate activation and ship size; in-pocket movement restrictions are untested.

rows.acceptance: A Remote Sensor Booster raises the target's scan resolution and lock range according to its script. A Remote Tracking Computer raises the target's turret optimal, falloff and tracking according to its script. Both are stacking-penalised, respect optimal/falloff, end on deactivation, and propagate logistics aggression flags.
rows.title: Remote sensor boosters & remote tracking computers
rows.why_missing: Only local ECCM/sensor boosters and TC/TE are rows; remote-assistance EWAR modules are absent.

rows.acceptance: An ARSB consumes cap booster charges instead of capacitor while loaded. An ARAR gives its repair bonus with nanite paste loaded. Both reload in 60 s and fall back to their unloaded behaviour.
rows.title: Ancillary remote shield boosters / armor repairers
rows.why_missing: The remote-shield/remote-armor rows ignore the charge-driven ancillary variants; only local ASB/AAR are covered.

rows.acceptance: Each cycle, every ship locking the user has a chance to lose its lock, based on its sensor strength versus the module strength (SDE attributes). The module's own self-penalties apply.
rows.title: Target Spectrum Breaker
rows.why_missing: No row covers this ECM-like defensive module group.

rows.acceptance: Activation grants the module's hull resistance bonus for its duration. The module then takes its burnout or damage per SDE attributes and respects its activation restrictions.
rows.title: Capital Emergency Hull Energizer
rows.why_missing: The capital defensive one-shot module is not covered by damage-control or hull-repairer rows.

rows.acceptance: While online, the module grants its additional locked-target slots and automatically locks eligible hostile targets per its attributes; the locks obey normal lock-time rules.
rows.title: Automated targeting system
rows.why_missing: There is no row for the auto-targeting module group; targeting-lock covers only manual locks.

rows.acceptance: marketProxy.GetMarketOrderHistory returns the character's fulfilled, expired and cancelled orders with state, final volume, price and timestamps, within the live retention window.
rows.title: Personal market order history
rows.why_missing: char-orders covers only active orders; the order history RPC has no behaviour row.

rows.acceptance: planetMgr.UserAbandonPlanet removes the command center, all pins, links and routes, destroys stored commodities, frees the colony slot and stops the simulation.
rows.title: Abandon planetary colony
rows.why_missing: PI rows cover building and simulation but not colony teardown.

rows.acceptance: NPC item traders exchange input items (and ISK, where specified) for output items exactly per itemtraderrecipes.fsdbinary, at the recipe's locations, consuming inputs atomically.
rows.title: NPC item trader recipes
rows.why_missing: The static recipe table ships with the client, but only the coarse feat:quasar.vendors row exists; there is no behaviour row.

rows.acceptance: map.GetSolarSystemVisits returns the character's per-system visit count and last-visit time, updated on every system entry.
rows.title: Personal system visit history
rows.why_missing: ui.map-stats covers global jumps/kills, not per-character visits.

rows.acceptance: Vanguard, Assault and Headquarters sites spawn only in systems with the matching role. Each has its fleet-size scaling, NPC waves and completion condition, and completion pays only fleet members on grid.
rows.title: Incursion site classes
rows.why_missing: Site-class behaviour is buried inside feat:pve.incursion-system.

rows.acceptance: Each militia's War HQ system (Mehatoor, Onnamon, Intaki, Amo) is identified by fwWarzoneSolarsystem.GetHQSystemIDs and hosts the HQ-only services (counter-insurgency outposts, militia facilities).
rows.title: Militia War HQ systems
rows.why_missing: GetHQSystemIDs is called by the client but no row specifies HQ semantics.

rows.acceptance: corpRegistry.UpdateDivisionNames renames the hangar and wallet divisions (Director only). The names persist and appear in hangars, wallets and ESI divisions.
rows.title: Division renaming
rows.why_missing: corp-hangars mentions names but has no write path or role check; wallet.corp-divisions is read-only.

rows.acceptance: ApplyToJoinFleet creates a pending request visible via GetJoinRequests to the boss and commanders, who can accept it (placing the member) or reject it with RejectJoinRequest. The applicant is notified either way.
rows.title: Fleet join requests
rows.why_missing: feat:fleet.fleet-advert lists the RPC but not the request review flow.

rows.acceptance: Jumping through a stargate into Zarzakh asks the pilot to confirm a toll. The toll scales with ship mass, roughly 10k ISK for small hulls up to about 100M ISK for the heaviest. It is debited and journaled only on confirmation; declining aborts the jump. Characters enlisted in a pirate militia (Angel Cartel or Guristas) pay nothing.
rows.title: Zarzakh gate toll
rows.why_missing: No navigation/stargate row covers per-system gate tolls; feat:navigation.stargate-jump only covers range, session change and cloak.

rows.acceptance: Entering Zarzakh by a gate locks the character to that gate for 6 hours; jumps out through any other Zarzakh gate are refused until it expires. Entering again through another gate resets the lock to the new gate. Leaving by the Deathless Shipcaster, a clone jump or a pod death is always allowed. The lock never affects entry from outside.
rows.title: Zarzakh emanation lock
rows.why_missing: The gate-lock timer is unique to Zarzakh and appears in no navigation or session-timer row.

rows.acceptance: Capital-sized hulls, including freighters but not the Orca, are refused at every stargate leading into Zarzakh, with the live UserError.
rows.title: Zarzakh capital gate restriction
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.jump-range-restrictions only covers capitals in high-sec; the Zarzakh freighter/capital gate ban has no row.

rows.acceptance: In Zarzakh, bookmark creation and warping to bookmarks are refused, and directional scans return the disabled error or empty result the live server gives. Both work again on leaving the system.
rows.title: Zarzakh bookmark and d-scan suppression
rows.why_missing: feat:scanning.dscan and feat:bookmarks.create have no system-level disable rule.

rows.acceptance: Ships in Zarzakh outside the Jovian safe zones (at the stargates, The Fulcrum and the Shipcaster) take periodic hull damage. Inside a safe zone no hazard damage is applied. The damage follows the normal damage/killmail pipeline.
rows.title: Zarzakh gravity hazard
rows.why_missing: No environmental hull-damage hazard is modelled anywhere in the ledger.

rows.acceptance: The Fulcrum refuses docking to characters enlisted in an Empire militia or carrying an active weapons or retribution timer. Neutral characters get repair, fitting, market, insurance and industry. Jump cloning needs a pirate-enlisted character, and corporation offices need a pirate-enlisted corporation. The Angel Cartel and Guristas LP stores are available there.
rows.title: The Fulcrum docking and alignment-gated services
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.npc-station-services uses station-operation services only; no row gates docking or services by militia alignment.

rows.acceptance: Manufacturing a sub-capital Angel Cartel or Guristas ship at The Fulcrum applies a 6% material and 70% time efficiency bonus. Pirate-enlisted characters also get a 90% SCC surcharge reduction, reflected in the job cost.
rows.title: Fulcrum pirate manufacturing bonuses
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.structure-rigs covers Upwell bonuses only; this NPC-facility, faction-specific bonus is untested.

rows.acceptance: Missile gate guns in Zarzakh attack capsuleers with a retribution timer and apply target painting and ECM. 'Zarzakh' and 'Outer Zarzakh' pirate NPC fleets patrol gates and stations in Zarzakh and the adjacent k-space systems, attacking non-pirate-aligned pilots and anyone with a retribution timer.
rows.title: Zarzakh gate guns and Deathless patrols
rows.why_missing: feat:npc.sentry-guns covers criminals/low standing only; alignment-based Deathless aggression and the retribution timer trigger have no row.

rows.acceptance: The Deathless Shipcaster in Zarzakh lets pirate-enlisted characters jump to their faction's Forward Operating Base in the current insurgency. Each warzone target has its own charge and cooldown, and non-pirate characters are refused.
rows.title: Deathless Shipcaster to insurgency FOB
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.shipcaster covers Empire militia landing pads only; the pirate shipcaster to the FOB is a separate destination and access rule.

rows.acceptance: Entry into each clade's Pochven home system needs at least 6.0 standing with the Triglavian Collective (V24 value). Lower-standing characters are refused at the gate with the live error. Internal and border systems have no standing gate.
rows.title: Pochven home-system standing gate
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.pochven-travel is a single coarse line; the standing-gated home systems are not testable from it.

rows.acceptance: Wormholes to and from Pochven spawn in k-space and wormhole systems. Their signature sits about 30 km from the actual wormhole, which is not deadspace. They open when scanned from the Pochven side. Guard NPCs differ by side: Triglavians outside, the Pochven NPC mix inside.
rows.title: Pochven entry/exit wormholes
rows.why_missing: Hidden inside feat:navigation.pochven-travel; the spawn and opening rules are untested.

rows.acceptance: A region-wide cyno jammer stops any cyno in Pochven, so jump drives can't enter. Capitals already inside may jump out. Capital ships can't use Pochven stargates, and capital manufacturing jobs in Pochven are refused.
rows.title: Pochven capital and cyno restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.cyno-jammer covers sov jammers only; the region-wide one-way rule and the capital gate/manufacturing bans have no row.

rows.acceptance: A medical clone can't be set in Pochven, and clone jumps into Pochven are refused. Clone bays in Pochven allow local clone swaps only.
rows.title: Pochven clone restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:clones.jump-clone-jump and feat:character.home-station have no regional exclusions.

rows.acceptance: Upwell structures can't be anchored in Pochven, though existing ones remain. A customs office can be anchored only by a pilot with at least 1.5 Triglavian standing.
rows.title: Pochven anchoring rules
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.anchor-restrictions covers distance and sec-band limits only, not region bans or standing-gated POCO anchoring.

rows.acceptance: Ships destroyed in Pochven drop up to 60% of their fitted and cargo items into the wreck, instead of the usual about 50% roll, and the killmail reflects the result.
rows.title: Pochven increased loot drop
rows.why_missing: feat:combat.wreck-loot fixes about 50% everywhere; the regional override has no row.

rows.acceptance: The deployable activates 1 minute after deploy and lasts 2 days; it can't be scooped. Any ship under 1,000,000,000 kg, friendly or hostile, can use it: after a 12-second warm-up it jumps 100 km in the ship's facing direction. There is no use cooldown and no limit on concurrent users.
rows.title: Mobile Micro Jump Unit
rows.why_missing: No row covers this deployable; the structures mobile-* rows stop at depot/tractor/cyno inhibitor/siphon/scan inhibitor/observatory.

rows.acceptance: Deployment needs Anchoring III and fleet membership. The beacon spools for 1 minute, then holds a cyno visible to the fleet for 60 minutes (the covert variant: 30 minutes, lower HP). It has its own HP and can be destroyed early, and it is single-use.
rows.title: Mobile Cynosural Beacon
rows.why_missing: Only ship-fitted cyno modules have rows; the deployable fleet beacon is absent.

rows.acceptance: The Mobile Observatory needs Anchoring III, deploys in 10 minutes and pings once deployment finishes, then every 10 minutes for up to 2 hours. Each ping gives each cloaked ship in the system that has passed its cloak stabilization timer an independent 40% chance to be decloaked. It can't be scooped, and it can't be deployed in high-sec, wormholes, deadspace or Abyssal space.
rows.title: Mobile Observatory decloak pings
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.mobile-observatory only says it 'shows cloaked ship presence within range', which doesn't match the live ping/decloak-chance mechanic.

rows.acceptance: Activating a cloak starts a 15-minute stabilization timer, which the cloaked pilot can see. While it runs the ship is immune to observatory decloak pings. It resets when the ship decloaks.
rows.title: Cloak stabilization timer
rows.why_missing: The cloak rows cover activation, decloak proximity and covert ops only; the stabilization timer has no row.

rows.acceptance: Deploying any mobile structure in a new-player starter or career-agent system is refused with the live 'restrictions in effect' error. Per-type distance rules apply, for example an MTU must be at least 5 km from another MTU and 50 km from stargates and stations. Attacking another pilot's mobile structure gives a suspect flag, not a criminal flag.
rows.title: Mobile structure deployment restrictions
rows.why_missing: The individual mobile-* rows don't specify system bans, distance rules or the suspect-only crimewatch outcome.

rows.acceptance: An MTU tractors and loots only wrecks and containers its owner may loot, closest first, and only while the owner is in the same system. It has no reinforcement, despawns after 2 days, and drops loot like a ship when destroyed.
rows.title: MTU ownership and operation rules
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.mobile-tractor only says it 'pulls wrecks and loots them'; the ownership, presence, ordering and lifetime rules are untested.

rows.acceptance: A deployed depot despawns with its contents after 30 days; any interaction resets the timer. It enters a 2-day reinforcement at 25% shield, but never while still anchoring. Scooping and redeploying does not repair it, so if it is still under 25% when attacked it is destroyed. Only the owner may access or scoop it.
rows.title: Mobile depot lifetime and reinforcement threshold
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.mobile-depot covers anchor time, refit and the reinforce duration, but not the lifetime, threshold or owner-only rules.

rows.acceptance: A CRAB deploys only in low/null. A capital ship must link to it for 4 minutes; during the link it can't warp, cloak or tether, and it gets a 10% universal resistance bonus. Activation then runs a 10-minute scan with waves of rogue drones. On success the special loot is restricted to the deployer and becomes open to all after 2 minutes, when the beacon self-destructs.
rows.title: CONCORD Rogue Analysis Beacon link and scan
rows.why_missing: No PvE row describes the CRAB deployable site.

rows.acceptance: Each character has Complex Encryption Qubits (CEQ), capped at 100, enough for 3 activations. Activations consume CEQ, which regenerates to full in about 22 hours. Each system's Signal Interference rises per CRAB until linking is refused (about 12 CRABs) and decays over about 25 hours.
rows.title: CRAB CEQ and system Signal Interference
rows.why_missing: This personal resource and the per-system throttle are server-side state with no ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Probe results show a cosmic signature's type/group from 25% signal strength and its site name from 75%. The site becomes warpable only at 100%. Below 25% only the signature ID and deviation are shown.
rows.title: Signature reveal thresholds
rows.why_missing: feat:scanning.probe-scan-math covers strength and deviation but not what information is revealed at each threshold.

rows.acceptance: All scan probes resolve cosmic signatures. Only combat probes also resolve ships, drones and structures. Wrecks, cargo containers and cloaked ships never appear in probe results.
rows.title: Core vs combat probe target classes
rows.why_missing: No row defines which object classes each probe type can resolve or the exclusions.

rows.acceptance: Core probes scan from 0.25 to 32 AU and combat probes from 0.5 to 64 AU, in power-of-two steps. Max deviation = base deviation × (range / base range) × (1 − 0.05×Astrometrics) × (1 − 0.05×Astrometric Pinpointing). Probes past their max flight time (RSS 16m40s, others 1h6m40s) return to cargo if there is room, otherwise they are lost.
rows.title: Probe scan range steps and max deviation
rows.why_missing: The scan-math, recall and skills rows don't fix the range limits, the deviation formula or the flight-time return/loss rule.

rows.acceptance: Signature difficulty levels are data-driven. Level I–III signatures resolve with the minimum strength of 42; Level IV needs a combined probe strength of at least 72, and Level V at least 104. Weaker probes can't reach 100% at any geometry.
rows.title: Signature difficulty minimum probe strength
rows.why_missing: No row ties signature difficulty to a probe-strength floor.

rows.acceptance: Starting a warp consumes capacitor = warpCapacitorNeed × ship mass × distance, reduced by Warp Drive Operation and SDE modifiers. With insufficient capacitor the warp is handled per V24 rules (shortened or refused), and capacitor updates reach the client.
rows.title: Warp capacitor cost
rows.why_missing: The plan (SP-3) requires a warp capacitor cost but no feat row tests it; feat:navigation.warp-to and warp-speed-formula omit capacitor.

rows.acceptance: Stargate jumps by carriers, dreadnoughts, FAX, supercarriers and titans are refused with the live UserError, as decided by the ship's SDE group/attributes. Freighters, jump freighters and sub-capital industrial command ships may use gates, subject to system-specific exceptions such as Zarzakh and Pochven.
rows.title: Capitals cannot use stargates
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.jump-range-restrictions only forbids capitals entering high-sec; the general gate ban is untested.

rows.acceptance: Each storm is centred on a null-sec system. Its core is the centre plus systems 1 jump away, with full effects; its periphery is systems 2–3 jumps away, with weaker effects. Extra storm PvE sites spawn only in the core. The centre moves one jump every 24–48h in a semi-random direction, avoiding retracing. Overlapping storms apply both effect sets.
rows.title: Metaliminal storm placement and movement
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.system-wide-effects only says storms apply dbuffs; the storm footprint, movement and site spawning are untested.

rows.acceptance: A Nosferatu cycle moves capacitor from the target to the user only when the target's capacitor is higher than the user's per the V24 comparison rule. Otherwise it moves nothing. The amount is capped by the module's drain amount and the user's free capacitor.
rows.title: Energy Nosferatu transfer rule
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.energy-neutralizer bundles neutralizers and Nosferatu in one parenthetical, hiding the conditional transfer rule.

rows.acceptance: The target's SDE resistance attributes scale incoming effect strength: sensor dampener resistance, weapon disruption resistance, target painter resistance, stasis webifier resistance, energy warfare resistance, remote repair impedance and remote electronic assistance impedance. Bastion/siege-style immunities set them to zero.
rows.title: EWAR and remote-assistance resistance
rows.why_missing: Each EWAR module row describes only the attacker side; no row tests target-side resistance or impedance.

rows.acceptance: NPCs apply webs, warp scramblers/disruptors, ECM, dampeners, tracking/guidance disruption, target painting and energy neutralizing at the strength, range, duration and chance given by their SDE entity attributes. The same target-side resistances and crimewatch-neutral rules apply.
rows.title: NPC EWAR from entity attributes
rows.why_missing: feat:npc.npc-ai-targeting folds 'weapons and EWAR' into one line with targeting and orbiting, the same coarse-row failure as the old 'mining' row.

rows.acceptance: NPCs with entity remote-repair attributes repair damaged members of their own spawn group (shield/armor) at the amount, range and cycle their attributes specify. Repairs stop when the NPC is jammed or out of range.
rows.title: NPC remote repair
rows.why_missing: Only feat:npc.sleepers mentions remote reps; there's no general NPC logistics row.

rows.acceptance: NPC AI picks and periodically re-evaluates targets among hostile ships and drones on grid, per V24 rules. New arrivals and drones can draw aggression, and targets switch on loss of lock, warp-out or destruction. Aggression lists are kept per NPC.
rows.title: NPC target selection and switching
rows.why_missing: Target switching is buried inside feat:npc.npc-ai-targeting with no separately testable acceptance.

rows.acceptance: Capital ship manufacturing jobs are accepted only in low/null-sec at structures with the required capital service (Azbel/Sotiyo class). Supercapital jobs additionally need a Sotiyo in sovereign null-sec with the Supercapital Construction Facilities sov hub upgrade online. Anywhere else, installation is refused with the live error.
rows.title: Capital and supercapital construction rules
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.install-job and structure-rigs have no location/upgrade gate for capital classes.

rows.acceptance: Creating a corporation project with an ISK reward escrows the pool from the chosen corp wallet division (role-gated). Each contribution pays its per-unit reward to the contributor until the pool or the per-character participation limit is exhausted. Payouts are journaled on both sides.
rows.title: Corporation project ISK reward pool
rows.why_missing: feat:corporation.corp-goals is a single 'create/contribute/claim' line hiding escrow, payout and limits.

rows.acceptance: A project ends when its target is reached, it expires, or an authorised member closes it. Remaining escrowed ISK is refunded to the source division. Unclaimed earned rewards stay claimable per V24 rules, and further contributions are refused.
rows.title: Corporation project close and expiry
rows.why_missing: Lifecycle termination and refunds are not part of feat:corporation.corp-goals acceptance.

rows.acceptance: Each contribution method the V24 client offers advances project progress only from server-observed events matching the project's filters, never from client-reported counts. Examples: kill NPCs, mine ore, manufacture items, deliver items, capture FW complexes, damage ships, earn LP.
rows.title: Corporation project contribution methods
rows.why_missing: 'progress matchers' in feat:corporation.corp-goals hides every method type behind one row.

rows.acceptance: A hacking board has a System Core, Defensive Subsystems (Firewall, Anti-Virus, Restoration Node, Virus Suppressor), Utility Subsystems (Kernel Rot, Polymorphic Shield, Secondary Vector, Self Repair) and Data Caches. Each has coherence and strength, set by difficulty and by the virus's analyzer/skill stats. Empty nodes show the distance (1–5) to the nearest core/utility/cache, and combat resolves per the V24 rules.
rows.title: Hacking board node behaviour
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.hacking-minigame is a single 'node-grid game' line covering every subsystem.

rows.acceptance: When the virus's coherence reaches zero the hack fails: the container locks out further attempts or self-destructs as the live server does, and ghost-site containers trigger their failure effects. A successful core kill opens the container or triggers the loot spew.
rows.title: Hacking failure outcome
rows.why_missing: No row states what happens when a regular hack fails; only ghost sites mention detonation.

rows.acceptance: Activating an abyssal filament leaves an Abyssal Trace at the origin, visible to others for the pocket duration. Except for PvP filaments, others can't follow. On completing the exit gate the ships return to the origin location. Pilots still inside when the timer ends are destroyed, including the capsule.
rows.title: Abyssal trace and return
rows.why_missing: The abyssal rows cover rooms, weather, tiers and gate activation, but not the origin trace or the return-to-origin rule.

rows.acceptance:
A conduit jump moves the conduit ship plus eligible fleet members within 10 km to the target cyno, for a flat isotope cost by conduit class (not mass-based).
- Black Ops: up to 30 ships, covert-ops-cloak-capable hulls only.
- Rorqual: up to 30 dedicated mining ships, and only while its Industrial Core is inactive.
- T1 carriers and supercarriers: 5–30 ships by Capital Jump Portal Generation level; command carriers double that.
- Eligible ships: shuttles, capsules, corvettes, frigates, destroyers, cruisers, battlecruisers and battleships.
- Titans cannot conduit jump.
- Members who opted out of conduit jumps are skipped.
rows.title: Conduit jump (Black Ops, carriers, supercarriers, Rorqual)
rows.why_missing: No ledger row covers conduit jumps. Only the auditor's fleet opt-in row mentions conduit at all, and jump-portal covers bridging only.

rows.acceptance:
Range and fuel:
- Max range per hull class follows the V24 table (e.g. dreadnought/carrier/FAX 3.5 ly, supercarrier/titan 3.0, JF/Rorqual 5.0, Black Ops 4.0); Jump Drive Calibration adds +20%/level.
- Isotope type follows the hull faction (Helium/Nitrogen/Oxygen/Hydrogen).
- Isotopes used = D × fuel/ly × (1 − 0.1×JFC) × (1 − 0.1×JF skill, JF only) × the stacking-penalised economizer terms.

Activation:
- Consumes 95% capacitor, minus 5% per Jump Drive Operation level.
- Refused inside a warp disruption bubble or when warp core strength is below 0.
- Alignment is not required.
rows.title: Jump drive range, isotope cost and activation constraints
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.jump-drive only says 'jump to a cyno within range consuming isotopes'. The range table, skill modifiers, fuel formula, capacitor cost and disruption gates are not testable from it.

rows.acceptance:
After a jump of L effective light-years:
- Fatigue = max(10×(1+L) min, existing fatigue×(1+L)), capped at 5 h.
- Jump activation cooldown = max((1+L) min, pre-jump fatigue/10), capped at 30 min.
- Fatigue decays in real time, offline included.

Effective distance reductions:
- Black Ops and the covert ships they bridge: −75%.
- Capsules, shuttles, haulers, blockade runners, DSTs, freighters, JFs, capital industrials and industrial command ships: −90%.

jumpTimers.GetTimers reports both timers.
rows.title: Jump fatigue and activation cooldown formula
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.jump-fatigue only says the timers 'grow per jump distance'. The minimum and multiplier formula, the caps and the per-class distance reductions are untested.

rows.acceptance:
Who and where:
- Normal cynos fit only on Force Recons and Black Ops.
- Refused in high-sec, within 200 km of a Mobile Cynosural Inhibitor, and in systems jammed by a Tenebrex or an incursion.
- Can be lit in wormhole space, but no jump drive can lock to it.

Activation:
- Requires fleet membership and speed below 500 m/s.
- The cyno is visible system-wide and on the map, and only fleet members can jump to it.

Cycle and fuel:
- Base cycle 10 min, halved on Recon/Black Ops (except Marshal).
- 500 Liquid Ozone per cycle, −10% per Cynosural Field Theory level; Force Recons get −80% fuel.

While lit:
- The ship's nominal speed is 0.
- It cannot dock or eject, but can self-destruct.
rows.title: Normal cynosural field lighting rules
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.cyno-field only says it 'lights a cyno for 5 min, consumes Liquid Ozone, fixes ship'. The location bans, hull restriction, speed and fleet gates, fuel math and dock/eject lock are not covered.

rows.title: Covert cynosural field rules
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.cyno-covert only says 'allow Black Ops and covert portals'. The visibility, jam-immunity, fitting and fuel rules are absent.

rows.title: Industrial cynosural field rules
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.cyno-industrial says 'JF and Rorqual only'. It omits Black Ops, the fitting restriction and the fuel cost.

rows.acceptance:
Titan bridges:
- go only to normal cynos or beacons and accept any subcapital;
- stay open 60 s, immobilise the titan, and cost 500 Strontium (modified by skill).

Black Ops bridges accept only covert-cloak-capable hulls; Rorqual bridges accept only mining ships. Both stay open 20 s and cost nothing to open.

For every bridge:
- Each jumper must be in fleet and within 2,500 m.
- Each jumper costs fuel = mass × portal mass factor × base cost × skill modifier × ly, taken from the bridger's fuel bay, then cargo.
- Ships in a bubble or warp-disrupted below 0 WCS cannot take the bridge; the host itself may be bubbled.
rows.title: Titan, Black Ops and Rorqual bridge rules
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.jump-portal is one line ('bridge fleet members to a cyno with fuel cost and range'). The per-class hull filters, durations, Strontium cost, mass-based fuel formula and bubble rule are hidden.

rows.acceptance: Ships arriving by jump drive or bridge materialise at a random point 5 km from the cyno or beacon. If they materialise inside a structure, they are ejected with velocity. If the cyno ship dies at the moment of the jump, the jump still happens and lands at the destination system's star.
rows.title: Jump drive arrival placement
rows.why_missing: Landing geometry for jump drives is not covered by any row; warp-landing-points only covers warps.

rows.acceptance:
Activation:
- An MJFG on a command destroyer spools for 9 s base, reduced 5% per level of Command Destroyers and of Micro Jump Drive Operation.
- It then jumps the CMDD and up to 25 capsuleer ships within 6 km by 100 km in the CMDD's facing direction.

Exclusions:
- Ships that are warp-scrambled or invulnerable (gate cloak, tether) are not moved.
- The CMDD itself cannot activate while scrambled.
rows.title: Micro Jump Field Generator (command destroyers)
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.micro-jump-drive mentions only a 'field variant jumps nearby ships'. The 25-ship cap, 6 km radius, spool reduction and exclusions are untested.

rows.acceptance: Battleship hulls with a Frigate Escape Bay can store one assembled frigate. When the battleship is destroyed, the pilot is placed into the stored frigate in space instead of a capsule. The frigate is not dropped as loot, and the killmail reflects that the frigate survived.
rows.title: Frigate escape bay
rows.why_missing: No ship or combat row mentions the escape bay. combat.ship-destruction always ejects a capsule.

rows.acceptance: An active weapons or PvP timer does not prevent jumping a wormhole; polarization still applies. A criminal with a pending CONCORD response is refused with the live 'mysterious technology' message. Aggression timers still block docking or tethering at citadels and refitting.
rows.title: Wormhole jumps ignore weapons timers but not CONCORD
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.weapon-timer says the timer blocks 'jumping' generically. The wormhole exemption and the CONCORD-pursuit refusal are untested.

rows.acceptance: Jump drives cannot target cynos in wormhole space and cannot jump from wormhole space to k-space cynos. Supercarriers and titans can never jump through any wormhole, whatever its remaining mass.
rows.title: Wormhole space jump drive and supercapital restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.wormhole-jump only enforces per-jump max mass. The w-space jump drive ban and the absolute supercapital ban have no row.

rows.title: Wormhole show-info text buckets
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.wormhole-lifetime only says 'size/age states visible'. The exact bucket thresholds and destination text are untested.

rows.acceptance: After exiting warp a ship is invulnerable and untargetable for a hidden 10 s, until it moves or starts locking a target. Filament activation during this window is refused with the 'ship is invulnerable' error. The window starts only after warp exit, so smartbombs hit during deceleration.
rows.title: Post-warp invulnerability
rows.why_missing: No navigation or dogma row covers the warp-exit invulnerability window.

rows.title: Session change timer triggers and blocking
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.session-change-timer is a vague 'per V24 rules'. The 10 s duration and the trigger list are not testable from it.

rows.title: Jump cloak immunities
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.gate-cloak only says '60 s cloak broken by moving'. The area-effect and proximity immunities are untested.

rows.acceptance:
Triggers:
- Offensive modules on capsuleers, Bastion activation and Command Burst activation start a 60 s weapons timer.
- Cycle weapons restart it each cycle.
- Persistent-effect modules (web, scram, damp, painter, bastion) hold it at 60 s until the effect ends.
- Command bursts expire it at cycle end.

While it runs, the character cannot:
- jump gates, dock or use acceleration gates;
- eject, store, refit or switch ships;
- tether.
rows.title: Weapons timer triggers and scope
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.weapon-timer only covers docking and jumping. The bastion and burst triggers, the persistent-module hold and the eject/refit/tether blocks are untested.

rows.acceptance: Shooting or being shot by a capsuleer starts a 15 min PvP timer. Being shot after disconnecting renews it, so the ship stays in space indefinitely. The NPC timer (5 min) is not renewed after logoff. An active PvP timer blocks filament activation.
rows.title: Capsuleer log-off timer renewal and filament block
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.legal-timers is 'Legal PvP aggression sets PvP timer'. The offline renewal, the asymmetry with the NPC timer and the filament block have no row.

rows.acceptance: A ship with a criminal timer in high-sec, or jumping into high-sec with one, cannot warp, jump, dock, eject, store or switch ships until it is destroyed. The capsule may then warp. CONCORD still destroys a ship that used session-change invulnerability even if the timer expired meanwhile.
rows.title: High-sec criminal movement lock
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.criminal-flag says only 'CONCORD and faction police respond'. The movement lock and the invulnerability-carryover rule are untested.

rows.title: Third-party assistance legality
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.logi-timers covers only timer inheritance. The offence class per target state and security band, and the burst filtering, are untested.

rows.acceptance: While a character holds a criminal timer, in any security band, the wrecks and jettisoned containers they own are automatically abandoned. Others can loot them without a suspect flag.
rows.title: Criminal jetcans and wrecks auto-abandon
rows.why_missing: No row covers ownership changes caused by criminal status; wreck-loot covers only the base drop chance.

rows.title: Low-sec offence classification
rows.why_missing: suspect-flag and criminal-flag are generic one-liners. The low-sec ship-vs-pod classification and the high-sec entry consequence are untested.

rows.acceptance:
Faction police engage capsuleers in ships when their security status is at or below a threshold that depends on system security:

| System security | Threshold |
|---|---|
| 1.0 | −2.0 |
| 0.9 | −2.5 |
| 0.8 | −3.0 |
| 0.7 | −3.5 |
| 0.6 | −4.0 |
| 0.5 | −4.5 |

Below the threshold, in that system:
- the character's cloak is disabled;
- docking or tethering in a ship is refused, while docking in a capsule is allowed;
- capsules are not attacked.
rows.title: Faction police thresholds per system security
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.faction-police says 'at −5', which contradicts the live per-security thresholds. The cloak, dock and pod rules are missing.

rows.title: Outlaw status
rows.why_missing: No crimewatch row defines the outlaw state or its assistance rule.

rows.acceptance: Security status gains from NPC kills (belt, mission and incursion rats) stop at +5.0. Clone soldier tags cannot raise security status above 0.0. Security status is clamped to −10..+10.
rows.title: Security status gain caps
rows.why_missing: sec-status-gain and sec-status-tags rows have no caps; the +5.0 NPC cap and the 0.0 tag cap are untested.

rows.acceptance: Any action that costs security status in high or low-sec makes every gate or station sentry on grid engage the offender for as long as they stay on grid. Aggression is not carried off-grid, and a new sec-loss act re-triggers it. Sentries are invulnerable and untargetable, and deal the live stats (500 km optimal).
rows.title: Sentry gun grid aggression
rows.why_missing: feat:npc.sentry-guns covers criminals and low standings only. The sec-loss trigger, grid reset and invulnerability are untested.

rows.acceptance:
Each clone soldier tag turned in at a low-sec CONCORD exchange adds +0.5 security status, but only within its band:

| Tag | Band |
|---|---|
| Trainer | −10 to −8 |
| Recruiter | −8 to −5 |
| Transporter | −5 to −2 |
| Negotiator | −2 to 0 |

A tag used outside its band is refused.
rows.title: Security tag tier bands
rows.why_missing: feat:crimewatch.sec-status-tags only says tags raise sec status; the per-tag bands are untested.

rows.acceptance: Clone soldier NPCs spawn in low-sec asteroid belts, with the pirate faction set by region and that faction's damage and resist profile. Transporters web at 10 km and Negotiators scram at 24 km. Each always drops its tier's security tag and pays its bounty.
rows.title: Clone soldier NPC spawns
rows.why_missing: No NPC row covers clone soldiers, the only source of security tags.

rows.acceptance:
Medium Upwell structures with an online service module enter armor reinforcement when shields are depleted. They exit at the owner's hour plus a period that depends on space, ±1.5 h jitter:

| Space | Exit after |
|---|---|
| Wormhole | 2.5 d |
| Null/low-sec | 3.5 d |
| High-sec | 4.5 d |
| War HQ | 24 h |

Large/XL structures exit after 24 h ±3 h.

These skip armor reinforcement and go straight to vulnerable armor:
- FLEX structures;
- abandoned structures;
- low-power Large/XL structures.
rows.title: Upwell armor reinforcement durations
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.reinforce-cycle bundles everything into 'timing per structure type and sec'. The per-space table and the skip conditions are untested.

rows.acceptance:
When armor is depleted, Large/XL structures enter hull reinforcement and exit after the owner's hour plus a period that depends on space, ±3 h:

| Space | Exit after |
|---|---|
| Wormhole | 1.5 d |
| Null/low-sec | 2.5 d |
| High-sec | 4.5 d |
| War HQ | 24 h |

Other structure classes:
- FLEX structures exit at the next chosen hour after 30 min ±30 min.
- Medium and abandoned structures have no hull timer, so their hull is immediately vulnerable.
rows.title: Upwell hull reinforcement durations
rows.why_missing: Hidden inside the coarse reinforce-cycle row; medium structures having no hull timer is a key rule that is untested.

rows.acceptance: A damaged structure starts a repair timer: 15 min in the shield and armor phases, 30 min in the hull phase. The timer pauses only while the structure takes damage of at least 10% of its damage cap, after resists. When it reaches zero, the structure fully repairs to full shields. The same rules apply to abandoned structures.
rows.title: Structure repair timer pause threshold
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.repair-timer says '15-min ... after ADM-like delay'. The 30 min hull timer and the 10% damage-cap pause rule are absent.

rows.acceptance:
A deployed structure has hull HP only:
1. It anchors for 15 min (paused while it takes at least 10% of its damage cap) and can be destroyed without timers.
2. It is then invulnerable for 24 h.
3. Inserting a quantum core starts a 15 min onlining timer, paused the same way. The structure is again killable without timers during onlining.
4. When onlining completes, structure, armor and shield are fully healed.
rows.title: Upwell anchoring and onlining phases
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.deploy-anchor says '24h anchoring then core', which misstates the live sequence. The pause rule and the no-timer vulnerability during anchoring and onlining are untested.

rows.acceptance:
Exit times for reinforcement:
- The owner sets the hour; the attacker determines the day.
- Exit times are computed from the moment the repair timer starts, not from the fight's duration.
- Jitter never rolls the exit over to the next day.
- The shield fight date fixes the dates of the later armor and hull timers.
rows.title: Reinforcement exit-time computation
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.vulnerability-schedule covers only setting the hour; the exit-time computation rules have no row.

rows.acceptance: An Upwell structure can be refitted only at full shields. Refit is refused while it is anchoring, onlining, repairing, under attack or reinforced.
rows.title: Structure fitting state locks
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.structure-fitting says only 'while not reinforced'; the full-shield and other state locks are untested.

rows.acceptance: Hacking an Upwell structure with a data analyzer reveals its owner-set reinforcement hour to the hacker. Without a successful hack, the hour is not exposed to non-members.
rows.title: Reveal reinforcement hour by hacking
rows.why_missing: No row lets attackers learn the reinforcement hour; hacking rows cover only containers.

rows.acceptance: Upwell structures are unaffected by ECM, dampeners, weapon disruptors, target painters, webs, warp disruption and energy neutralisers. Activating such modules on them has no effect, per the live server.
rows.title: Structures immune to EWAR
rows.why_missing: The EWAR module rows never exclude structures as targets.

rows.title: Tether eligibility and blocked actions
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.tether and tether-break cover invulnerability and lock or aggression breaks. The eligibility conditions (core, abandoned, fighters, unpiloted), the module-specific breaks and the blocked actions while tethered are untested.

rows.acceptance: Each Mercenary Den needs one level of Mercenary Den Management, so dens per character are at most the skill level. A den anchors only within 10 km of a temperate planet's Orbital Skyhook. It is owned and managed by one character, not a corporation, and the sov owner may charge a tax.
rows.title: Mercenary Den anchoring and ownership
rows.why_missing: feat:sovereignty.mercenary-den is one coarse line ('anchor on skyhooks, generate infomorphs, can be attacked'). The skill cap, planet type and personal ownership are untested.

rows.acceptance: Development and Anarchy both rise over time on an online den. Higher Development raises the hourly Infomorph Decryption Key yield. Completing generated Mercenary Tactical Operations raises Development and lowers Anarchy. At Anarchy level 2 (about 8 days), the den siphons the host skyhook's workforce away from the sov owner.
rows.title: Mercenary Den development and anarchy
rows.why_missing: Neither the mercenary-den row nor the mercenary-tactical-ops row defines the two indices, their effects or the workforce siphon.

rows.acceptance: An attacked den enters a 24 h reinforcement with a 6 h window and is inaccessible while reinforced. Its shields must be repaired to 50% afterwards. On destruction, each stack of stored Infomorph Decryption Keys has a 50% drop chance.
rows.title: Mercenary Den reinforcement and destruction loot
rows.why_missing: 'Can be attacked' in the coarse row hides the timer, access lock, repair threshold and loot rule.

rows.title: Abyssal entry ship and filament counts
rows.why_missing: The abyssal rows cover rooms, tiers, weather and the trace, but not the hull-class and filament-count entry rules.

rows.title: Abyssal filament activation restrictions
rows.why_missing: No row lists the filament activation gates.

rows.acceptance:
System security limits filament tiers:
- 1.0 and 0.9 allow only T0.
- 0.8 to 0.5 allow higher tiers without a flag up to a security-dependent tier: T3 at 0.8, T4 at 0.7, T5 at 0.6, T6 at 0.5.
- Activating a tier above that limit in high-sec gives the activator a suspect flag.
rows.title: Abyssal tier by system security and suspect flag
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.abyssal-tiers covers difficulty and loot only; the security gating and suspect table are untested.

rows.title: Abyssal in-pocket restrictions
rows.why_missing: No abyssal row specifies these restrictions or the downtime handling.

rows.acceptance:
Arrival and gate:
- Ships arrive 35–70 km from the pocket gate.
- The gate unlocks only when every NPC in the pocket is dead.

NPCs:
- Abyssal NPCs leave no wrecks, pay no bounty and cost no faction standing.

Loot:
- The Triglavian Bioadaptive Cache (300 HP) drops the pocket loot.
- Extraction nodes and subnodes (T1+) roll their limited loot pool, and may be empty.
rows.title: Abyssal pocket clearing, cache and NPC rules
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.abyssal-gates only names the RPCs; the unlock condition, no-bounty/no-standing rule and cache loot are untested.

rows.acceptance:
Placement:
- New characters are placed in their school's NPC starter corp.
- Leaving a player corporation places the character in the default NPC corp for their bloodline.
- Enlisting in faction warfare as an individual places them in the faction's FW NPC corp.

Players cannot apply to NPC corps, and a character that leaves its starter corp can never return to it.
rows.title: NPC corporation placement rules
rows.why_missing: feat:corporation.leave-corp and fw.enlist do not specify the destination NPC corp rules or the no-return rule for starter corps.

rows.acceptance: Overloaded modules accumulate heat in their rack (high/mid/low) per cycle; heat dissipates exponentially when no modules in the rack are overloaded; module heat damage probability and amount scale with current rack heat percentage, slot adjacency distance, and the pilot's Thermodynamics skill (-5% heat damage per level).
rows.title: Rack heat buildup, dissipation, and Thermodynamics skill
rows.why_missing: feat:fitting.overheat coarsens rack heat accumulation/dissipation curves, slot-adjacency distance attenuation, and the Thermodynamics skill bonus into a single summary.

rows.acceptance: dogmaIM.RepairModule and StopRepairModule consume Nanite Repair Paste from the ship's cargo hold proportional to module HP repaired and module base cost, repair damaged (non-burnt-out) offline modules over time scaled by the Nanite Operation skill, and refuse to repair completely burnt-out modules.
rows.title: In-space module repair nanite paste consumption and repair rate
rows.why_missing: feat:fitting.module-damage-repair lumps station repair service and in-space nanite paste repair together without testing paste consumption formula, Nanite Operation skill scaling, or burnt-out module rejection.

rows.acceptance: Tech II frequency crystals, faction frequency crystals, and mining crystals with crystalVolatilityChance and crystalVolatilityDamage roll volatility damage each cycle via OnCrystalDamage, track per-crystal HP, and destroy the loaded crystal when its damage reaches 1.0 HP.
rows.title: Tech II and faction crystal volatility and destruction
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.turret-laser mentions T2/faction crystal degradation alongside basic laser firing, hiding the per-crystal volatility roll, damage tracking, and crystal destruction mechanics.

rows.acceptance: Titan Phenomena Generators (Amarr/Caldari/Gallente/Minmatar) apply their racial system/grid-wide fleet dbuff effects to ships for the cycle duration, consume Strontium Clathrates, and prevent the Titan from warping or jumping for the duration.
rows.title: Titan Phenomena Generators
rows.why_missing: Titan Phenomena Generators have no feature row in modules.

rows.acceptance: superWeaponMgr.ActivateConeModule fires a Bosonic Field Generator cone doomsday along the chosen directional vector, dealing damage over ticks to all ships inside the cone geometry after the warmup delay and immobilizing/tether-blocking the Titan.
rows.title: Bosonic Field Generator cone AoE doomsday
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.doomsday only lists ActivateSinglePointTargetedModule and ActivateSlashModule, omitting ActivateConeModule (Bosonic Field Generator).

rows.acceptance: superWeaponMgr.ActivateSpatialModule teleports ships within the target sphere to a random point in the system, and superWeaponMgr.ActivateMultiPointModule sweeps a beam path between start and end points damaging ships along the arc.
rows.title: Spatial Phenomena Generator (GTFO) and Reaper doomsdays
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.doomsday omits ActivateSpatialModule and ActivateMultiPointModule.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Clone Vat Bay on a Titan or Rorqual consumes Liquid Ozone, immobilizes the ship for the cycle, and allows fleet members to install or jump to clones in the ship only while the module is active.
rows.title: Clone Vat Bay activation and Liquid Ozone consumption
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.clone-vat-bay and feat:clones.jump-clone-ship-bay omit the active cycle requirement, Liquid Ozone consumption, and ship immobilization.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Zero-Point Mass Entangler on a Heavy Interdiction Cruiser reduces the ship's mass by up to 80% for wormhole traversal while reducing maximum velocity and disabling Microwarpdrives and Micro Jump Drives while active.
rows.title: Zero-Point Mass Entangler
rows.why_missing: The HIC Zero-Point Mass Entangler module for wormhole mass reduction has no feature row.

rows.acceptance: Heavy Stasis Grapplers apply maximum velocity reduction at 0-1 km and decay effectiveness linearly across their optimal and falloff ranges down to a minimum web floor.
rows.title: Heavy Stasis Grappler distance-based effectiveness decay
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.stasis-webifier mentions grapplers only in passing, hiding the distance-dependent web strength falloff formula.

rows.acceptance: Fitting any Polarized turret or missile launcher sets all shield, armor, and hull resistances of the ship to 0% regardless of hardeners, rigs, or Damage Control modules.
rows.title: Polarized weapon resistance zeroing
rows.why_missing: Polarized weapons' override of ship shield/armor/hull resistances to 0% is not covered by any feature row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Micro Jump Field Generator on a Command Destroyer spools for 6s (reduced by Micro Jump Drive Operation), blooms signature radius, and translates up to 25 non-warp-scrambled ships (including drones, bombs, and probes) within 6 km 100 km along the Command Destroyer's heading vector.
rows.title: Micro Jump Field Generator (Command Destroyer boosh)
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.micro-jump-drive lumps the personal MJD and the AoE Command Destroyer MJFG together, hiding the 25-entity cap, 6 km radius, scram exclusion per ship, and bomb/probe translation.

rows.acceptance: Incoming remote shield/armor repair on a target scales with remote assistance impedance when multiple capital/subcapital remote repairers cycle on the same ship within the impedance window.
rows.title: Capital remote repair diminishing returns (remote assistance impedance)
rows.why_missing: Remote assistance impedance diminishing returns on stacked remote repairs has no feature row.

rows.acceptance: Capital Micro Jump Drives jump a capital ship 250 km forward after spool-up, and Capital Micro Jump Field Generators on Lancer Dreadnoughts/Carriers jump up to 50 subcapital ships within 10 km 250 km forward.
rows.title: Capital Micro Jump Drive and Capital Micro Jump Field Generator
rows.why_missing: Capital MJD and Capital MJFG (250 km jump, 50-ship cap) have no feature row.

rows.acceptance: Support fighter squadrons apply warp disruption (Siren), stasis webification (Dromi), sensor dampening/target painting (Cenotaph), or ECM (Scarab) via fighterMgr.CmdActivateAbilitySlots, with squadron size scaling the EWAR strength.
rows.title: Support fighters (Scarab, Siren, Dromi, Cenotaph)
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.fighter-abilities lumps all fighter classes together, hiding support fighter EWAR strength scaling with remaining squadron size.

rows.acceptance: fighterMgr.ExecuteActivateAbilitySlotsOnPoint fires a heavy fighter's point-targeted AoE bomb ability at the specified 3D coordinate in space, consuming a bomb charge from the squadron and dealing AoE damage at detonation.
rows.title: Long-range heavy fighter AoE bomb ability
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.fighter-abilities covers target-locked abilities (CmdActivateAbilitySlots), omitting positional AoE abilities (ExecuteActivateAbilitySlotsOnPoint).

rows.acceptance: Recalled fighter squadrons in carrier/supercarrier/structure fighter tubes repair damaged fighter HP, replace destroyed fighters from the fighter bay, and reload depleted ability charges over per-unit reload timers before relaunch.
rows.title: Fighter tube refueling, rearming, and repairing
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.fighter-squadron-losses mentions refilling squadron size from bay, but omits tube repair time and ability charge rearming timers.

rows.acceptance: Immobile sentry drones (IsSentry) have zero max velocity, ignore CmdReturnHome orbit movement, and can only be returned to the drone bay when the controlling ship is within 2,500 m.
rows.title: Sentry drone 2500m scoop requirement
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.sentry-drones states sentries are immobile, but omits the 2,500 m proximity requirement to recall/scoop them into the drone bay.

rows.acceptance: Augmented/faction drones (e.g. Gecko, Praetor/Infiltrator/Valkyrie/Berserker/Wasp/Ogre/Hammerhead/Hobgoblin/Hornet/Acolyte/Warrior variants) and mutaplasmid-mutated abyssal drones apply their multi-type or mutated dogma damage, tracking, velocity, and HP attributes in combat.
rows.title: Multi-damage, augmented, and abyssal mutated drones
rows.why_missing: Multi-damage/augmented and mutaplasmid-mutated drone combat attribute resolution has no dedicated row.

rows.acceptance: Launched missiles exist as destiny balls with HP, velocity, and flight time (explosionDelay * agility/mass); missiles that exceed flight time before reaching the target or are destroyed by smartbombs/defender missiles deal zero damage.
rows.title: Missile ball lifetime, smartbomb destruction, and outrunning
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.missile-launchers and feat:modules.missile-application do not test missile flight time expiration (outrunning missiles) or smartbomb AoE destruction of in-flight missiles.

rows.acceptance: Void bombs neutralize capacitor in AoE, Lockbreaker bombs break target locks in AoE, and Focused Void/Scorch bombs apply capital-scaled AoE neutralization/damage with explosion radius vs target signature radius scaling.
rows.title: Void, Lockbreaker, and Focused Void bomb effects
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.bomb-launcher bundles damage, Void, and Lockbreaker bombs into a single row without testing AoE capacitor neutralization, lock breaking, or bomb-to-bomb damage resistance.

rows.acceptance: Wreck types carry their SDE accessDifficulty modifier (frigate/cruiser/battleship/capital, Tech I vs Tech II, Sleeper); salvaging fails when the salvager module + Salvaging skill + rigs yield <= 0% access chance, and T2/Sleeper wrecks drop T2/Sleeper salvage tables.
rows.title: Wreck salvage access difficulty and T2/Sleeper wreck requirements
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.salvager does not distinguish T1, T2, capital, and Sleeper wreck access difficulty or T2/Sleeper salvage loot tables.

rows.acceptance: Attackers who applied 0-damage EWAR (warp disruption, web, ECM, neut, damp, painter) or damage within the 15-minute aggression window before ship destruction are recorded in the killmail attackers list with their ship, weapon/module type, and damage done, while attackers older than 15 minutes are pruned.
rows.title: Killmail EWAR participation and 15-minute aggression window
rows.why_missing: feat:combat.killmail-generate does not specify zero-damage EWAR participation or the 15-minute aggression expiry window.

rows.acceptance: ship.SelfDestruct on a capsule in space destroys the capsule after the countdown (2 minutes), destroys active implants, generates a pod killmail (if aggressed within 15 minutes), and respawns the character in their home station medical clone.
rows.title: Capsule self-destruct in space
rows.why_missing: feat:ships.self-destruct tests ship self-destruct, and feat:character.self-destruct-clone tests docked home_station.self_destruct_clone, leaving in-space capsule self-destruct untested.

rows.acceptance: An active 60s Weapons Timer prevents tethering to Upwell structures, activating any filament, refitting modules in space, boarding/ejecting ships in space, and storing ships in a Ship Maintenance Bay.
rows.title: Weapons timer blocks tethering, filaments, refitting, and ship swap
rows.why_missing: feat:dogma.weapon-timer only mentions blocking docking and jumping, omitting filament activation, in-space refitting, tethering, and SMB storage.

rows.acceptance: Activating high-tier Abyssal filaments in high-security space (0.5-1.0) is either blocked in 0.8-1.0 or applies a 15-minute Suspect flag upon exiting the Abyssal trace per V24 security band rules.
rows.title: High-sec Abyssal filament tier restrictions and suspect flag
rows.why_missing: High-sec Abyssal filament security band restrictions and exit suspect flagging are not covered by feat:navigation.filament-abyssal.

rows.acceptance: Activating an Abyssal filament spawns an Abyssal Trace ball at the entry point in the origin solar system that is scannable with combat probes, allows fleet members (for 2x/3x frigate/destroyer runs) to enter, and despawns when the run finishes or the 20-minute pocket timer expires.
rows.title: Abyssal trace in-space beacon and collapse
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.filament-abyssal does not cover the persistent Abyssal Trace ball in the origin system or its combat-probe scannability and collapse.

rows.acceptance: Entering an Abyssal trace in a Destroyer consumes 2 filaments from the fleet activation and allows up to 2 Destroyers in fleet; entering in a Frigate consumes 3 filaments and allows up to 3 Frigates, multiplying loot cache drops accordingly.
rows.title: Co-op Abyssal Deadspace (2x Destroyer / 3x Frigate filament consumption)
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.filament-abyssal mentions 1-3 ships but does not specify the 2-filament Destroyer / 3-filament Frigate cost or loot multiplier.

rows.acceptance: Ships flying outside the spherical boundary of an Abyssal Deadspace room take escalating omni structural damage per tick until they return inside the arena or are destroyed.
rows.title: Abyssal pocket arena boundary damage
rows.why_missing: Abyssal pocket out-of-bounds boundary damage is not covered in feat:pve.abyssal-pocket.

rows.acceptance: The Encounter Surveillance System lives behind an acceleration gate inside a 75 km intrusion bubble that blocks warping, Microwarpdrives, Micro Jump Drives, cloaking, and cyno lighting within the ESS grid.
rows.title: ESS deadspace grid bubble, warp, MWD, MJD, and cloak restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.ess covers main bank linking and theft, omitting the ESS acceleration gate and 75 km intrusion bubble restrictions.

rows.acceptance: Every 2h45m, if the ESS Main Bank is not currently being hacked, its accumulated ISK is automatically distributed to the wallets of the characters who contributed ratting bounties during that cycle in proportion to their contributions.
rows.title: ESS Main Bank 2h45m auto-payout distribution
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.ess mentions 'payout to owners' coarsely without specifying the proportional ratting contributor auto-payout cycle.

rows.acceptance: ESS Reserve Bank keys are bound to a specific null-sec quadrant and 15-minute or 45-minute unlock duration; essMgr.RequestUnlockReserveBank consumes a matching quadrant key and streams ISK payouts over the key's duration to linked ships on grid.
rows.title: ESS Reserve Bank key quadrant & duration tiers
rows.why_missing: feat:pve.ess-reserve omits quadrant key matching and the 15m/45m timed payout stream.

rows.acceptance: A job's Estimated Item Value (EIV) is computed as the sum of (base ME-0 blueprint material quantity * adjusted market price) per run from the server's adjusted price table, unaffected by blueprint ME level or structure material bonuses.
rows.title: Estimated Item Value (EIV) calculation from blueprint base materials
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.job-cost references EIV in passing, without specifying how EIV is derived from ME-0 base materials and adjusted prices.

rows.acceptance: Installing an industry job charges the SCC surcharge (percentage of EIV credited to SCC) and, when the installer is in Alpha clone state, an additional Alpha clone facility tax percentage, each recorded as a separate wallet journal entry.
rows.title: SCC industry surcharge and Alpha clone industry tax
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.job-cost mentions SCC surcharge in passing and completely omits the Alpha clone industry tax.

rows.acceptance: Manufacturing Tech II, Faction, Capital, and Supercapital hulls consumes their SDE-defined advanced/capital components, Neurolink Protection Cells, Core Temperature Regulators, and PI/reaction intermediates without hardcoded recipes.
rows.title: Capital, T2, and faction ship multi-stage component manufacturing
rows.why_missing: Multi-stage capital/supercapital/faction hull manufacturing recipes from SDE blueprints.fsdbinary have no dedicated verification row.

rows.acceptance: Standup M-Set and L-Set manufacturing, research, invention, and biochemical/composite/hybrid reactor rigs multiply their ME, TE, and cost bonuses by the solar system's security band multiplier (high-sec vs low-sec vs null-sec/WH) and reject high-sec installation for reaction rigs.
rows.title: Upwell Standup industry/reaction rig security band multipliers
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.structure-rigs does not test the high/low/null security band multipliers or reaction rig high-sec restrictions.

rows.acceptance: Deploying a Command Center requires the matching Command Center type for the planet's type (Barren, Gas, Ice, Lava, Oceanic, Plasma, Storm, Temperate; Shattered planets forbid PI colonies), and only the 5 R0 resources native to that planet type can be extracted.
rows.title: Planet type Command Center matching and resource availability
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.command-center and feat:pi.planet-info omit planet-type Command Center matching, Shattered planet prohibition, and per-planet-type R0 resource sets.

rows.acceptance: planetOrbitalRegistryBroker anchors a Customs Office Gantry at an unowned non-high-sec planet, upgrades it to a Player Owned Customs Office with a Customs Office item, and enforces a single shield reinforcement timer before destruction.
rows.title: Customs Office Gantry deployment, upgrade, and POCO reinforcement
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.customs-office and feat:pi.poco-settings cover tax rates and settings, but omit Customs Office Gantry anchoring, upgrade to POCO, and POCO reinforcement/destruction.

rows.acceptance: Orbital transfers via a Spaceport Launchpad allow up to 10,000 m3 both ways (import and export) at 1x POCO tax rate without cooldown, whereas Command Center launches export up to 500 m3 into an orbital container at 1.5x tax rate.
rows.title: Spaceport Launchpad vs Command Center orbital transfer volume & tax
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.launch and feat:pi.customs-office do not distinguish Spaceport Launchpad bidirectional orbital transfer vs Command Center one-way container launch and their different volume/tax multipliers.

rows.acceptance: PlaceBuyOrder, PlaceMultiSellOrder, and ModifyCharOrder validate that order prices conform to EVE's 4-significant-figure tick size rule (e.g. 1234000.0 valid, 1234567.89 rejected) and reject non-conforming prices.
rows.title: Four-significant-figure market price tick validation
rows.why_missing: feat:market.place-buy, feat:market.place-sell, and feat:market.modify-order do not specify the 4-significant-digit price tick rule.

rows.acceptance: ModifyCharOrder charges the V24 relist fee equal to max(0, price_increase) * broker_fee_rate + new_order_value * relist_discount_factor * broker_fee_rate, where relist_discount_factor is reduced by the Advanced Broker Relations skill (6% per level).
rows.title: Order modification relist fee formula and Advanced Broker Relations
rows.why_missing: feat:market.modify-order mentions 'relist fee' without specifying the V24 relist fee formula or the Advanced Broker Relations skill reduction.

rows.acceptance: Corporation buy orders debit escrow/broker fees from the chosen corp wallet division and deliver filled items to the corp's Market Deliveries division at the destination station/structure; corp sell orders sell from a chosen corp hangar division and credit proceeds minus sales tax to the chosen corp wallet division.
rows.title: Corporation market order division routing and delivery
rows.why_missing: feat:market.corp-orders does not specify corp hangar division selection or delivery of corp buy orders to the Market Deliveries hangar flag.
