rows.acceptance: Basic, Advanced, and High-Tech factories require installing a matching schematic (P0->P1, P1->P2, P2->P3, P3->P4); input commodities must be explicitly routed from storage/extractors to factory inputs, and output commodities routed to storage or launchpads; factories idle with UserError if inputs are depleted or output destination is full.
rows.title: Planetary factory schematic routing and commodities production
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.factory-cycles only checks that cycles run; explicit commodity route configuration, schematic assignment, and buffer blockage rules are not specified.

rows.acceptance: Transferring commodities between a planetary launchpad and a Planetary Customs Office (POCO) assesses export/import taxes: tax = commodity base market value * quantity * tax rate; NPC POCO applies 10% base tax; player-owned POCO applies corporation tax rate with standing discounts; transfers fail if character cannot pay required ISK.
rows.title: Planetary Customs Office import and export taxation
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.customs-office only mentions tax rate lookup; the actual tax formula based on commodity tier base values and transfer execution is absent.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Cynosural Field Generator consumes Liquid Ozone fuel based on ship hull and Cynosural Field Theory skill; creates a celestial cynosural beacon ball visible system-wide on the overview; the activating ship is completely immobilized (speed 0 m/s) and cannot dock, jump, or cloak for the 5-minute cycle duration.
rows.title: Cynosural Field Generator beacon spawning and ship immobilization
rows.why_missing: No row models cynosural beacon ball creation, Liquid Ozone consumption, or the 5-minute immobilization lock.

rows.acceptance: Covert Cynosural Field Generators activate on Stealth Bombers, Force Recons, Blockade Runners, and Black Ops hulls without consuming Liquid Ozone; creates a covert cynosural beacon visible only to fleet members; duration is 1 minute; permits jumping and bridging by Black Ops and Covert Jump Portals.
rows.title: Covert Cynosural Field beacon generation for Black Ops
rows.why_missing: Covert cyno mechanics (zero fuel, fleet-only visibility, 1-minute cycle, covert portal targeting) are completely missing from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Activating jump drive consumes racial isotope fuel per light-year jumped based on ship type and Jump Fuel Conservation skill; jump activation adds a Jump Activation Cooldown timer and scales Jump Fatigue minutes: fatigue = (current fatigue * 0.1 max 10 min + 1) * (1 + distance_ly * ship_fatigue_multiplier); jump is refused if jump range exceeds ship maximum.
rows.title: Capital ship jump drive fuel consumption and fatigue accumulation
rows.why_missing: feat:ships.jump-drive is a generic query row; the exact isotope consumption math and the exponential Jump Fatigue formula are not in any testable row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Jump Portal Generator on a Titan or Black Ops battleship targeting a fleet cynosural beacon opens a spatial jump portal bridge; consumes isotope fuel per jumping fleet ship based on ship mass and distance; subcapital fleet members within 2,500m of the bridge ship can activate the portal to jump directly to the beacon.
rows.title: Titan and Black Ops Jump Portal bridging
rows.why_missing: Jump Portal bridging mechanics (bridge generation, per-passenger mass fuel consumption, 2,500m bridge proximity) have no ledger row.

rows.acceptance: An anchored Upwell structure requires installing a Quantum Core item matching its hull type (Astrahus, Fortizar, Keepstar, Raitaru, Azbel, Sotiyo, Athanor, Tatara) into its dedicated core room; service modules cannot be brought online without a core installed; upon structure destruction, the Quantum Core drops with 100% certainty in the structure wreck.
rows.title: Upwell structure Quantum Core onlining gate and guaranteed drop
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.quantum-core is a 1-line row; the service module onlining dependency and guaranteed 100% wreck drop are not specified.

rows.acceptance: Items entering Asset Safety wrap into an asset safety container and start a 20-day transit timer to the nearest NPC station (or same-system NPC station); claiming delivered items in the same system charges a 0.5% estimated item value fee; claiming items after lowsec transit charges a 15% item value fee; items in wormhole structures drop as loot instead of entering asset safety.
rows.title: Asset safety transit timer and ISK recovery fees
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.asset-safety-auto is coarse; the 20-day timer, the 0.5% same-system fee, and the 15% remote fee are not testable in any existing row.

rows.acceptance: When an Upwell structure enters an armor or hull vulnerability window, an uninterrupted 15-minute repair timer begins; if attackers fail to apply damage exceeding the damage cap threshold to pause the timer, the repair timer counts down to 0, repairing all shields and armor back to 100% and returning the structure to Shield Vulnerable status.
rows.title: Upwell structure 15-minute vulnerability repair window
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.repair-timer mentions repair vaguely; the damage pause threshold, the 15-minute countdown, and the full shield/armor restoration are not specified.

rows.acceptance: Energy Vampire (Nosferatu) modules transfer capacitor from target to host ship only if the target's absolute capacitor energy (in GJ) is higher than the activating ship's current capacitor energy, unless the activating ship has a Blood Raider hull bonus (Cruor, Ashimmu, Bhaalgorn) which overrides this limitation and drains target capacitor down to 0 GJ; transfer occurs at the end of the module cycle.
rows.title: Energy Vampire (Nosferatu) absolute capacitor threshold and Blood Raider override
rows.why_missing: Capacitor warfare in the ledger does not specify the target-greater-than-user absolute cap requirement, end-of-cycle transfer timing, or the Blood Raider hull exception.

rows.acceptance: Energy Neutralizer modules deduct activation cost from user capacitor at cycle initiation and immediately drain neutralizing energy from the target ship's capacitor at cycle initiation (modified by distance falloff E = E0 * 0.5^(((d - opt) / falloff)^2) and target capacitor battery resistance); if target capacitor is less than neutralized amount, target capacitor is drained to exactly 0 GJ without underflowing.
rows.title: Energy Neutralizer cycle initiation drain, falloff, and zero-cap clamping
rows.why_missing: The ledger lacks a row for Energy Neutralizer cycle start cap drain, falloff scaling, and target capacitor zero-clamping behavior.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Target Painter increases target ship signature radius by Sig_effective = Sig_base * (1 + sum(Bonus_i * StackingPenalty_i)), where stacking penalty follows S(n) = e^(-(n-1)^2 / 26.7); signature increase immediately updates incoming missile damage and turret tracking equations against the painted target.
rows.title: Target Painter signature radius bloom formula and stacking penalties
rows.why_missing: Target painting signature bloom formula, stacking penalty application, and instant damage formula recalculation are absent from all EWAR rows.

rows.acceptance: Remote Sensor Dampeners (unscripted or loaded with Targeting Range Dampening Script) reduce target's max targeting range by module bonus percentage with stacking penalties; target locks already active beyond the newly reduced max range are preserved until broken, but attempting new locks beyond the reduced range fails.
rows.title: Remote Sensor Dampener targeting range reduction and active lock preservation
rows.why_missing: Sensor dampener targeting range reduction, scripting bonus doubling, and retention of existing locks are not specified in the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Remote Sensor Dampeners (unscripted or loaded with Scan Resolution Dampening Script) reduce target ship scan resolution with stacking penalties; target lock acquisition time scales inversely according to t_lock = 40000 / (ScanRes * (arcsinh(Sig))^2) (bounded by 0.25s server tick minimum).
rows.title: Remote Sensor Dampener scan resolution lock time penalty
rows.why_missing: Scan resolution dampening effect on targeting lock time formula is completely omitted from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Weapon Tracking Disruptors loaded with Optimal Range Disruption Script (or unscripted) apply percentage reduction to target turret optimal range and falloff distance with stacking penalties, shifting the turret hit probability curve inward.
rows.title: Weapon Tracking Disruptor optimal range and falloff disruption
rows.why_missing: Tracking disruptor optimal and falloff disruption is not differentiated or tested in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Weapon Tracking Disruptors loaded with Tracking Speed Disruption Script (or unscripted) apply percentage reduction to target turret tracking speed with stacking penalties, dramatically decreasing turret hit chance and critical hit chance against targets with high angular velocity.
rows.title: Weapon Tracking Disruptor tracking speed disruption
rows.why_missing: Turret tracking speed reduction math under tracking disruption is absent from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Missile Guidance Disruptors reduce target missile velocity and flight time (when loaded with Missile Range Disruption Script) or reduce explosion velocity and increase explosion radius (when loaded with Missile Precision Disruption Script) with stacking penalties, degrading applied missile damage against small or fast targets.
rows.title: Missile Guidance Disruptor range and precision disruption
rows.why_missing: Missile Guidance Disruptor mechanics (range and precision disruption scripts) have no matching row in the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Burst Jammer pulses an area-of-effect ECM wave affecting all uncloaked ships (friendly, hostile, and neutral) within its effect radius (5km T1, 6km T2); rolls independent jam chance against each ship's sensor strength; breaking target locks on jammed ships and flagging the activating pilot suspect/criminal if unprovoked neutral targets are affected in High/Low security space.
rows.title: Burst Jammer AoE radius, friendly-fire mechanics, and Crimewatch flags
rows.why_missing: Burst Jammer AoE radius mechanics, friendly-fire lack of discrimination, and Crimewatch flagging are omitted from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Overloading an active module increases rack heat each cycle according to t = -ln(1 - H) / (heatAttenuation * sum(heatAbsorptionRateModifier)), raising rack heat towards 100%; module receives duration or attribute boost (e.g. 50% speed for prop mods, 20% tackle range, 10% repair amount and -15% repair cycle time).
rows.title: Overheating rack heat generation formula and module performance multipliers
rows.why_missing: Overheating rack heat generation formula and module performance multipliers are not represented in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Each overheated module cycle rolls a chance of heat damage based on current rack heat level; damage is applied to the module and conducts to adjacent slot positions in the same rack with falloff based on slot distance (without wrapping around rack edges); Thermodynamics skill reduces heat damage taken by 5% per level.
rows.title: Heat damage probability scaling and adjacent slot propagation
rows.why_missing: Heat damage probability scaling with rack heat and distance-based heat propagation to neighboring slots are absent from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: When a module's heat damage accumulates to 100% of its structure hitpoints (typically 40 HP), the module burns out: it immediately deactivates, goes offline, cannot be reactivated or offlined/onlined in space, and disables any module group it belongs to until repaired or ungrouped.
rows.title: Module burnout state transition, automatic offlining, and group disabling
rows.why_missing: Module burnout state transition, automatic offlining, and module group breakage are not specified in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Selecting Repair on a heat-damaged module in space consumes Nanite Repair Paste from cargo over time; repair rate and paste consumption scale with module volume, Thermodynamics, Nanite Operation (-5% paste/level), and Nanite Interfacing (+20% repair rate/level); fully burned-out modules cannot be repaired in space with paste and require docking or Upwell structure tethering.
rows.title: In-space Nanite Repair Paste consumption and burned-out repair restrictions
rows.why_missing: In-space nanite repair paste consumption formulas, skill modifiers, and burned-out module repair restrictions have no ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Natural shield recharge follows the differential rate dC/dt = (10 * C_max / tau) * (sqrt(C / C_max) - C / C_max), where recharge rate reaches its maximum of 2.5 * C_max / tau at exactly 25% current shield capacity, falling towards 0 as capacity approaches 0% or 100%.
rows.title: Passive shield recharge rate non-linear curve peaking at 25%
rows.why_missing: The non-linear 25% peak shield and capacitor recharge curve differential equation is not explicitly tested by any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Shield Booster modules consume capacitor and apply their full shield hitpoint restoration instantly at the beginning of the module activation cycle (t = 0), entering cooldown for the remainder of the cycle duration.
rows.title: Shield Booster instant boost application at cycle initiation
rows.why_missing: Shield booster cycle-start boost application timing is not specified or contrasted with armor repairers in the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Armor Repairer modules consume capacitor at the start of activation (t = 0) but apply armor hitpoint restoration only upon cycle completion (t = tau_cycle); if the activating ship is destroyed or module is knocked offline before cycle end, zero armor hitpoints are restored.
rows.title: Armor Repairer delayed repair application at cycle completion
rows.why_missing: Armor repairer end-of-cycle repair timing and cancellation on premature destruction/offlining lack a testable row.

rows.acceptance: Remote Armor Repairers and Remote Shield Transporters apply 100% repair amount within optimal range; beyond optimal range, applied repair decays exponentially according to 0.5^(((distance - optimal) / falloff)^2), dropping to ~50% at optimal + falloff and 0% beyond optimal + 3*falloff.
rows.title: Remote Armor and Shield repair optimal and falloff effectiveness curve
rows.why_missing: Remote repair optimal and falloff effectiveness falloff mechanics are absent from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Ancillary Armor Repairers (AAR) loaded with Nanite Repair Paste repair 3x the normal armor amount per cycle while consuming 1 unit of paste per cycle; when paste runs out, the module continues to cycle repairing only 1x base armor amount; initiating a reload triggers a mandatory 60-second reload cycle.
rows.title: Ancillary Armor Repairer Nanite paste consumption and 3x repair multiplier
rows.why_missing: Ancillary Armor Repairer 3x paste multiplier, capless/cap-consuming paste mechanics, and 60s reload timer are omitted from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Ancillary Shield Boosters (ASB) loaded with Cap Booster charges (Navy or standard) consume 1 cap booster charge per cycle and 0 capacitor energy; when empty, the module continues cycling by consuming large capacitor energy per cycle; initiating a reload triggers a 60-second reload cycle.
rows.title: Ancillary Shield Booster charge consumption, zero-cap operation, and reload lock
rows.why_missing: Ancillary Shield Booster charge consumption, zero-cap operation while loaded, and 60s reload lock have no ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Deactivating a cloaking device triggers a sensor recalibration delay timer (governed by module cloaking delay attribute and Cloaking skill level, -10% delay per level); during this delay, the ship is completely blocked from initiating targeting locks on any space entity; Stealth Bombers and Covert Ops hulls have role bonuses reducing this delay to 0 seconds.
rows.title: Cloak deactivation sensor recalibration targeting delay and Stealth Bomber exemption
rows.why_missing: Decloak sensor recalibration targeting lock delay and Stealth Bomber 0s delay exception are not in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Prototype Cloaking Device or Improved Cloaking Device immediately reduces the ship's maximum sub-warp velocity by 90% or 75% respectively; the velocity limit is enforced until cloak deactivation; Covert Ops Cloaking Devices incur 0% velocity penalty.
rows.title: Standard Cloaking Device sub-warp velocity penalty enforcement
rows.why_missing: Cloaking sub-warp velocity reduction penalties (75% / 90%) and Covert Ops exemption are absent from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: A warp disruption bubble located along a ship's warp path within 500 km behind the destination celestial drags the ship out of warp at the bubble edge (drag bubble); a bubble placed directly in front of the destination along the warp vector stops the ship on the near perimeter of the bubble (catch/stop bubble); ships with Interdiction Nullification active ignore drag and catch effects.
rows.title: Warp disruption bubble 500km vector drag and catch anchor points
rows.why_missing: Warp bubble 500km vector drag and forward catch anchor calculations are not defined in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Micro Jump Drive spools for 12 seconds (reducible by Micro Jump Drive Operation skill); warp scrambler (scram) applied during spool cancels the jump; upon completion, ship jumps exactly 100 km forward in the direction of its current heading vector while preserving sub-warp speed and alignment.
rows.title: Micro Jump Drive 12-second spool, scram cancellation, and 100km vector jump
rows.why_missing: Micro Jump Drive 12-second spool-up, scram cancellation, and 100km vector jump execution lack a dedicated testable row.

rows.acceptance: Applying a Warp Scrambler (short point) applies 2 points of warp disruption strength and immediately deactivates running Microwarpdrives (MWD) and Micro Jump Drives (MJD), preventing their reactivation while scrambled; Warp Disruptors (long point) apply only warp disruption without shutting off propulsion modules.
rows.title: Warp Scrambler MWD and MJD propulsion shutdown vs Warp Disruptor
rows.why_missing: The distinction between warp disruption (warp block only) and warp scrambling (immediate MWD/MJD deactivation) is not captured in any ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Launching drones from drone bay verifies that total bandwidth of launched drones does not exceed the ship hull's drone bandwidth attribute (e.g. 50 Mbit/s for cruisers) and total number of active drones does not exceed 5; launching additional drones beyond bandwidth or count limit is refused with UserError.
rows.title: Drone bay bandwidth allocation and maximum active 5-drone control limit
rows.why_missing: Ship hull drone bandwidth limits and active 5-drone control caps are not covered in any drone ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Sentry drones deploy into space with velocity 0 m/s and cannot accept move or orbit commands; sentry drones acquire targets and fire turrets using standard turret tracking math based on target angular velocity and distance relative to the stationary sentry drone ball.
rows.title: Sentry drone zero-velocity immobility and stationary turret tracking math
rows.why_missing: Sentry drone zero-velocity immobility and stationary turret tracking calculations lack a testable row.

rows.acceptance: NPC combat entities periodically evaluate threat priority and switch aggro from player ship to active player drones based on drone signature radius, proximity, and DPS output; attacking drones take damage and can be recalled to bay to shed NPC aggro.
rows.title: NPC threat priority evaluation and aggro switching onto player drones
rows.why_missing: NPC threat priority and aggro switching onto player drones is omitted from PvE and drone ledger rows.

rows.acceptance: A ship tethered to an Upwell structure receives passive shield, armor, and hull repair and cannot be targeted or damaged; tether immediately breaks if the ship activates an offensive module, acquires a weapons timer, starts target locking an entity, or moves beyond the structure's docking perimeter.
rows.title: Upwell structure tethering protection, repair, and weapons timer breaking
rows.why_missing: Upwell structure tethering protection rules, weapons timer breaking conditions, and repair effects are absent from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Smartbomb module inflicts instantaneous area-of-effect damage of its specified damage type to all uncloaked entities (ships, drones, missiles, probes) within its spherical radius (up to 5,000m for Large Smartbombs) without requiring target locks; applying smartbomb damage to unprovoked neutral entities in High/Lowsec triggers Crimewatch suspect/criminal flags and CONCORD intervention.
rows.title: Smartbomb area-of-effect omnidirectional damage and Crimewatch flagging
rows.why_missing: Smartbomb AoE sphere damage application, lack of target lock requirement, missile/drone destruction, and Crimewatch flagging have no testable row.

rows.acceptance: Activating an Interdiction Nullifier module grants immunity to warp disruption bubbles (mobile warp disruptors, warp disrupt probes, and warp disruption field generators) for its active duration, allowing warp initiation from inside bubbles and preventing drag/catch bubble effects; incurs passive penalties to ship drone bandwidth, scan resolution, and targeting range while fitted.
rows.title: Interdiction Nullifier module active bubble immunity and passive fitting penalties
rows.why_missing: Active Interdiction Nullifier module activation, bubble immunity window, and passive fitting penalties are missing from the ledger.

rows.acceptance: Activating an Energy Nosferatu module transfers capacitor from the locked target to the activating ship only when the activating ship's current capacitor percentage is strictly lower than the target ship's capacitor percentage; if the activator's capacitor percentage is equal or higher, the module cycles without draining or transferring capacitor, unless the ship possesses a hull role bonus (e.g. Blood Raider hulls: Cruor, Ashimmu, Bhaalgorn, Sentinel, Curse) which overrides the percentage restriction and permits drain regardless of relative levels.
rows.title: Energy Nosferatu target-relative capacitor drain and Blood Raider override
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.energy-neutralizer bundles Nosferatu in parentheses as 'and nosferatu transfer to self' without specifying or testing the critical capacitor percentage threshold rule or the Blood Raider hull bonus override.

rows.acceptance: Fitting a Stasis Grappler module is restricted strictly to Battleship, Capital, and Industrial Capital hulls (maximum 1 per ship); upon activation on a locked target within range, it applies an intense speed reduction (up to 85% at point-blank 1km) that decays over a wide falloff curve according to the standard falloff equation factor = 0.5^(((distance - optimal)/falloff)^2) rather than standard webifier sharp cutoffs.
rows.title: Stasis Grappler inverse falloff velocity reduction and hull restrictions
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.stasis-webifier mentions 'grapplers' in half a sentence, but does not capture the Battleship/Capital fitting group restriction, the 1-per-ship limit, or the unique extended falloff curve.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Covert Jump Portal Generator on a Black Ops battleship opens a covert jump portal bridging fleet members to a Covert Cynosural Field; the portal verifies that each jumping fleet member is piloting an eligible covert-capable hull (Stealth Bomber, Covert Ops Frigate, Force Recon, Blockade Runner, Strategic Cruiser with Covert Subsystem) and rejects non-covert hulls; consumes isotope fuel from the Black Ops cargo per jumping ship's mass and jump distance in light-years.
rows.title: Covert Jump Portal Generator covert-capable ship filtering and isotope consumption
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.jump-portal bundles Titan and Black Ops portals together without specifying or testing the covert-hull restriction, Covert Cyno target requirement, or per-ship mass fuel consumption formula.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Mining Foreman Burst module on an industrial command ship (Orca, Rorqual, Porpoise) consumes one charge (Mining Laser Optimization, Mining Laser Field Enhancement, or Mining Equipment Preservation) and emits an area-of-effect wave affecting all fleet members within range who have fleet boosts enabled; applies the specific timed duration buff to target ships' mining lasers, strip miners, ice harvesters, or crystal residue probabilities.
rows.title: Mining Foreman Burst module charge types, AoE propagation, and duration buffs
rows.why_missing: feat:mining.mining-fleet-boosts was flagged fake because the codebase used a test-only fleetBoost: true kwarg without bursts, charges, or dbuffs; the charge consumption, AoE wave, and duration buff mechanics have no dedicated row.

rows.acceptance: Fleet commanders and designated squad/wing leaders can assign alphanumeric tags (letters A-Z, numbers 1-9) to locked entities via fleetProxy.SetTargetTag; assigned tags are broadcast to all fleet members on grid and persist in the overview, tactical display, and fleet target window until untagged or target destruction.
rows.title: Fleet target tagging with letters and numbers
rows.why_missing: feat:fleet.fleet-broadcasts only specifies broadcast commands (target, align, need armor), but target tagging (assigning and displaying tactical letters/numbers across the fleet) is a distinct system with its own client RPCs and notifications.

rows.acceptance: Salvaging a yellow (unowned) player or NPC wreck in Highsec or Lowsec with a Salvager module or Salvage Drone does not trigger Crimewatch suspect flags or aggression timers, allowing legal salvage by third parties; in contrast, opening and taking items from the cargo of a yellow wreck or container flags the looting pilot as a Suspect for 15 minutes.
rows.title: Wreck salvaging legality without suspect flag vs cargo theft
rows.why_missing: feat:combat.wreck-loot and feat:modules.salvager do not capture the legal distinction between salvaging unowned wrecks (legal, no flag) and looting unowned wrecks (suspect flag).

rows.acceptance: Activating an Emergency Hull Energizer (EHE) on a capital ship (Carrier, Dreadnought, Supercarrier, Titan) grants 95% resistance to all damage types (EM, Thermal, Kinetic, Explosive) on the hull layer for a short duration (e.g. 20-25 seconds); the module burns out completely upon cycle completion regardless of heat damage, cannot be repaired with nanite repair paste in space, and cannot be refitted while damaged.
rows.title: Emergency Hull Energizer invulnerable hull resistance burst and burn-out
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.assault-damage-control covers sub-capital Assault Damage Controls, but capital Emergency Hull Energizers have unique burn-out mechanics (mandatory module destruction upon activation, non-repairable in space).

rows.acceptance: Carriers and Supercarriers launch fighters through dedicated launch tubes (3 tubes for Carriers, 5 tubes for Supercarriers); launching requires active launch tube assignment, verifies squadron fighter count against launch tube limits, and forbids launch while cloaked, in warp, or tethered; recalled squadrons land back in the specific launch tube and refuel/restock charges.
rows.title: Carrier and Supercarrier fighter launch tubes and hangar capacity
rows.why_missing: feat:drones.fighter-abilities and feat:drones.fighter-movement cover movement and abilities, but the carrier launch-tube architecture (3/5 tube limits, tube assignment, and restocking) has no row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Proving Grounds filament enters the character or fleet into the proving grounds matchmaking queue via pvpFilamentMgr.JoinPVPQueue; validates ship hull class, module tier restrictions, and implant restrictions; upon match found, creates an isolated proving arena pocket bounded by a boundary sphere; exiting the sphere or exceeding the arena timer inflicts escalating environmental damage until destruction.
rows.title: Proving Grounds filament matchmaking queue, ship restrictions, and arena boundaries
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.filament-pvp only covers joining queue, while arena pocket instantiation, ship/module validation rules, boundary sphere enforcement, and timer environmental damage lack a testable row.

rows.acceptance: Installing an optional Decryptor item into an invention job applies exact SDE dogma attribute modifiers to the resulting T2 blueprint copy: modifies the base invention success probability (e.g. +40%, -20%), alters the output BPC max runs (e.g. +1 to +9 runs), and adjusts starting Material Efficiency (-2 to +3) and Time Efficiency (-4 to +6); rejected decryptors that do not match the item's race/group raise validation errors.
rows.title: Invention decryptor run count, ME/TE delta, and base probability scaling
rows.why_missing: feat:industry.decryptors only states 'decryptors apply modifiers', but does not test the exact formula combining base probability, decryptor chance multiplier, and run count additions.

rows.acceptance: Transferring commodities through a Customs Office (POCO or NPC CO) calculates tax from commodity estimated base value (EIV per tier: P0=5, P1=400, P2=7200, P3=60000, P4=1200000); NPC CO tax base is 10% reduced by Customs Code Expertise skill down to 5%; POCO tax applies the player owner's corp/alliance/standing tax rates set in POCO configuration and is debited from character wallet directly to POCO owner corporation wallet.
rows.title: Player-Owned and NPC Customs Office tax computation based on commodity tier and standing
rows.why_missing: feat:pi.customs-office and feat:pi.poco-settings exist at high level, but the exact tax formula per commodity tier (P0..P4 EIV), Customs Code Expertise skill reduction, and wallet transfer routing lack a specific testable row.

rows.acceptance: Deploying a Mobile Depot in space requires launching from cargo at least 5km from other structures/celestials; initiates a 60-second anchoring countdown during which it is invulnerable; once anchored, ships within 2,500m of the depot can access its fitting service to refit modules and change rigs/subsystems in space; when attacked, entering 0% shield triggers a 48-hour reinforced timer before structure HP becomes vulnerable.
rows.title: Mobile Depot 1-minute anchoring timer, reinforcement cycle, and fitting perimeter
rows.why_missing: feat:fitting.fitting-service-space covers the fitting check, but Mobile Depot physical anchoring (60s deployment, 5km distance rule, and 48h reinforcement timer) has no ledger row.

rows.acceptance: Invoking repairshop.GetQuotes returns repair cost calculations for all damaged items (ship hull, armor, damaged modules, and damaged drones) based on base item value and missing HP percentage; invoking repairshop.RepairItems debits ISK from the character wallet, clears all damage attributes, and restores structure/armor and module HP to 100%.
rows.title: Repairshop service damage estimation and ISK repair execution
rows.why_missing: Station repair services are mentioned in general feat:structures.station-services, but the repairshop quotation RPC, item list filtering, cost formulas, and damage attribute clearing have no testable row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Triglavian Mutadaptive Remote Armor Repairer on a friendly target heals armor with a continuous cycle spool-up; each uninterrupted cycle on the same target increases the armor repair amount by a multiplier (up to the maximum spool multiplier, e.g. 150% additional repair) until cycling stops or target changes.
rows.title: Triglavian Mutadaptive Remote Armor Repairer continuous cycle repair spool-up
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.remote-armor notes 'mutadaptive spool-up for Triglavian' in parentheses in a shared row with all remote armor reps, but the cycle count tracking, spool multiplier ceiling, and target-switch reset are untested.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Triglavian Entropic Disintegrator (Supratidal, Meson, Vorton) against a target applies continuous cycle damage that scales upward with each consecutive cycle (by 5% per cycle up to a maximum multiplier of 150% to 250% base damage); the spool bonus immediately resets to 0% if the target is lost, cycle deactivates, target moves beyond maximum range, or capacitor empties.
rows.title: Triglavian Entropic Disintegrator continuous fire damage spool-up and target loss reset
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.turrets covers standard projectile/hybrid/laser weapons, but the unique Triglavian continuous-fire damage spooling mechanic and reset conditions have no dedicated row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Standup Point Defense Battery module on an Upwell structure discharges rapid pulses of area-of-effect damage in a sphere around the structure (e.g. 5,000m to 10,000m radius); inflicts damage to all hostile drones, light fighters, and incoming missiles within the sphere; damages unshielded capsules and frigates that enter the defense perimeter.
rows.title: Upwell structure Standup Point Defense Battery AoE damage against drones and missiles
rows.why_missing: feat:structures.structure-weapons aggregates all structure weapons in one coarse row, omitting the specialized anti-drone/anti-missile PDS pulse mechanics and friendly-fire exclusions.

rows.acceptance: Jumping through an active player-owned Ansiblex Jump Gate via structureJumpBridgeMgr.CmdJumpThroughStructureStargate consumes Liquid Ozone from the gate structure's fuel bay based on jumping ship mass and jump distance; unlike capital jump drives, ships jumping through an Ansiblex do not accumulate Jump Activation Index or Jump Fatigue timers; ships with active weapons timers or ships exceeding jump gate mass limits are refused.
rows.title: Ansiblex Jump Gate jump fatigue exemption and liquid ozone consumption
rows.why_missing: feat:navigation.ansiblex-jump and feat:navigation.jump-fatigue exist separately, but the crucial rule that Ansiblex gates provide fatigue-free transit while consuming structure ozone and checking weapons timers lacks a testable row.

rows.acceptance: Activating a Titan Lance Doomsday (superWeaponMgr.ActivateSlashModule) projects an untargeted linear beam in the Titan's forward orientation vector extending 300km; after a 15-second warmup during which the Titan cannot move or steer, the beam fires an energy wave that deals massive damage to all ships within the beam cone, applies a 5-minute jump/warp suppression debuff to hit ships, and disables the Titan's warp and jump drives for the doomsday cycle duration.
rows.title: Titan Lance Doomsday directional beam vector, AoE damage cone, and warp suppression
rows.why_missing: feat:modules.doomsday lists both single-target and lance doomsdays in one line, but the 300km beam vector geometry, cone collision, warmup lock, and 5-minute warp suppression debuff are not covered.

rows.acceptance: Corp titles and title assignments, member roles and scoped roles, role history, shares/shareholders, medals (created and issued), votes and ballots, hangar/wallet division names, member limits, bulletins, recruitment ads, friendly-fire setting and employment history read back identically via corporation/ESI calls after a server restart, and an aborted transaction leaves none of them changed.
rows.title: Corporation governance state survives restart

rows.acceptance: Character/corp/alliance contacts and labels, blocked lists, People & Places notes, mailing lists, mail read/deleted flags and labels, player-created chat channels (MOTD, operators, password, bans/mutes), calendar events and responses, and bookmark folders/subfolders are unchanged after a server restart, and the same values are seen through the game client and ESI.
rows.title: Contacts, mail state, chat channels, calendar and bookmark folders survive restart

rows.acceptance: Notifications already received stay in the notification list after a server restart, and notifications created while a character was offline (or just before a restart) are delivered at the next login. Notification IDs are never reused.
rows.title: Notifications persist and offline notifications are delivered after restart

rows.acceptance: PI colony pin/link/route layouts and customs-office settings, running moon extractions and Metenox moon miners (with their timers), observer mining ledgers, R&D agent accumulated research points, and industry job cost/facility tax metadata are unchanged after a restart. Timers keep counting through downtime.
rows.title: PI layouts, moon drilling, R&D agents and industry metadata survive restart

rows.acceptance: Character and corp wallet journals (with timestamps), market transactions, corp wallet transactions, regional market price history and market-order metadata are unchanged after a restart. Corp bills, autopay, direct player trades and HyperNet raffles keep their state and escrowed ISK/items, so no ISK is lost or duplicated.
rows.title: Market and wallet history, order metadata and escrowed player trades survive restart

rows.acceptance: Corporation LP wallets and character LP reward logs report the same balances and entries after a server restart. An LP store purchase that fails leaves LP, ISK and items all unchanged.
rows.title: Corporation LP balances and LP logs survive restart

rows.acceptance: War lifecycle timers, surrender negotiations, mutual-war invites and peace treaties, alliance applications and lifecycle data, FW system occupancy/victory points/advantage and character FW stats, sov campaign scores, prospecting indices, skyhook reagent stock, and insurgency campaign phase and corruption/suppression all read back identically after a restart.
rows.title: War, FW, sov and insurgency progress survives restart

rows.acceptance: Cosmic signatures and anomalies keep their IDs and positions across a restart until they despawn naturally. Escalation bookmarks, incursion state, epic arc progress and mission metadata are kept. A character inside an Abyssal pocket at restart is restored with the pocket timer still running, or ejected the way the live server does it, without losing the ship silently.
rows.title: Exploration sites, escalations, Abyssal pockets and mission/arc progress survive restart

rows.acceptance: After a restart, fitted modules (including Upwell service modules) keep their online/offline state, weapon banks stay grouped, secure-container passwords, ALSC locks and logs, and ship access configs still apply, and a paused skill queue stays paused with no SP gained.
rows.title: Module online state, weapon groups, container passwords/ALSC and skill-queue pause survive restart

rows.acceptance: Security-status transaction history, the safety setting, drone settings, Zarzakh gate lockouts, wormhole polarization timers and structure docking denials are unchanged after an unscheduled restart. Criminal/suspect/limited-engagement timers either keep counting or expire exactly as they would on the live server, so a crash never clears a flag early.
rows.title: Security status history, safety, criminal flags and lockouts are not reset by a crash

rows.acceptance: Omega subscription expiry, redeemed codes, entitlements and accepted agreements, season points and challenge progress, Project Discovery rank/XP/kredits, and daily alpha-injector cooldowns are unchanged after a restart. A redeemed code cannot be redeemed again after a restart.
rows.title: Account entitlements, season points and Project Discovery progress survive restart

rows.acceptance: Contacts, mail labels and deleted mail, custom item names, CSPA charges, war records, alliances and PLEX balances read the same through the game client, ESI and Quasar at any moment, and still match after a restart. No service keeps a parallel in-memory copy that can diverge from the world DB.
rows.title: One authoritative copy per piece of state (client, ESI and Quasar agree)

rows.acceptance: When a mutating RPC fails (handler error or persistence error), every observable store (world DB tables, snapshot fields, mining ledger, and any service runtime state) is exactly as it was before the request. A randomized fault-injection test finds no partial updates.
rows.title: A failed request leaves no state change anywhere

rows.acceptance: After a crash while Siege/Bastion/Triage, a reactive armor hardener, overheating or remote-rep spool is active, the restarted server shows the ship and module attributes at their un-buffed fitted values (heat aside, if the live server persists it). No resonance or bonus written by an active cycle stays on the item.
rows.title: Transient module effects never outlive their cycle across a restart

rows.acceptance: IDs allocated for alliances, corporations, notifications, reports and every other persisted entity are strictly greater than any ID allocated before a restart. Creating an alliance after a restart never overwrites an existing alliance.
rows.title: Entity IDs are never reused after restart

rows.acceptance: With a character in an abyssal pocket who disconnects (or never calls any abyssal RPC), when 1200 s pass the server destroys the ship and capsule through the death pipeline without any client RPC: ship item destroyed, killmail written, capsule destroyed, character respawned at the medical clone, abyssal state cleared. Verified by advancing the clock with no client calls, then logging in.
rows.title: Abyssal timer expiry while disconnected destroys ship and pod

rows.acceptance: After a server restart (or downtime) with a character inside an abyssal pocket, on next login the character is in the filament origin system at a random point (live downtime rule), or still in an intact pocket with the original collapse time. Never stranded in 32000001 with NotInAbyssalPocket. Pocket state is in the world DB, not the PVE_SPECIAL_STATE static.
rows.title: Abyssal pocket survives restart or returns the pilot to the origin

rows.acceptance: A solar system that contains dynamic balls (logged-off ships within their timer, abandoned drones, NPCs, wrecks/cans with despawn timers, active modules) keeps advancing simulation and timers when no session is subscribed. Test: leave a disconnected ship being shot by NPCs in a system with no other sessions; its HP keeps dropping and its logoff timer and despawn timers expire on schedule.
rows.title: Systems keep simulating with no observers

rows.acceptance: On server start, every persisted in-space object (jetcans, wrecks with remaining lifetime, anchored containers and deployables, structures, and ships still inside their logoff window) is re-materialized as a ball at its saved position in its system actor. Test: create one of each, restart, and SetState/AddBalls for that system shows them with the same itemIDs and positions.
rows.title: Persistent space objects are reloaded into the ballpark after restart

rows.acceptance: At the daily downtime job, uncompleted mission dungeons with killed NPCs are reset, so their spawn waves are present again on the next warp-in.
rows.title: Mission NPCs respawn after downtime

rows.acceptance: When the controlling ship warps, docks, takes a gate/wormhole/jump-drive, logs off (clean or disconnect) or is destroyed, every non-abandoned DroneSpaceState with that parent ship is set is_abandoned=true, target cleared, drone balls stop in place and stop counting against the ship's bandwidth/max-drones. Owner can CmdReconnectToDrones from any ship on the same grid; any other pilot can ScoopToDroneBay. Test: launch 2 drones, CmdStargateJump, assert LaunchDrones in new system succeeds for 5 drones and CmdReturnBay does not return the left-behind drones.
rows.title: Drones left in space on warp/dock/jump/logoff/disconnect/ship death become abandoned

rows.acceptance: Drone items with location_id=solarSystemID are re-materialized as balls (from persisted item_positions) with an abandoned DroneSpaceState after restart, so they can be scooped/reconnected; no drone item is ever left in a system with no ball. Test: launch drone, restart (reload sqlite), assert drone ball exists and ScoopToDroneBay works.
rows.title: Drones in space survive server restart

rows.acceptance: entity.CmdReturnBay/CmdReturnHome/CmdEngage only act on drones whose solar_system_id equals the session system and are within control range; drones in another system are never moved into the bay. Test: launch, dock or jump, call CmdReturnBay, assert item stays in space.
rows.title: Drone recall restricted to same system/grid

rows.acceptance: Launching moves the fighter item out of the tube into space (location=solarSystem); on carrier dock/jump/logoff/death squadrons become abandoned (balls persist, tubes freed, items not counted as in the ship, not rolled by loot fairy); CmdScoopAbandonedFighterFromSpace recovers them; state survives restart. Test: launch, dock, assert item not in station and tube re-launch works after scoop.
rows.title: Fighter squadrons left in space on dock/jump/logoff/carrier death

rows.acceptance: weapon/pvp/suspect/criminal expiries, pending CONCORD, limited engagements, NPC timers, disapproval and safety level are stored in the world DB (not ServerContext/static) and reloaded; lazily expired on read. Test: set criminal flag, restart, GetClientStates still reports criminal with original expiry.
rows.title: Crimewatch flags/engagements survive server restart

rows.acceptance: check_crimewatch_action_restriction (or equivalent) is invoked by warp, CmdStargateJump, WormholeJump and jump drive/bridge/portal handlers: non-capsule ship with criminal timer in sec>=0.45 gets an error on warp/gate jump; any active weapons timer blocks WH jump and jump drive. Test each handler.
rows.title: Hisec criminal cannot warp or jump gates; weapons timer blocks WH and jump-drive jumps

rows.acceptance: On ship death the victim (if online) receives OnSessionChanged with shipid=new capsule and a 10s session-change timer is recorded; on pod death the victim receives the session change to the medical-clone station (stationid/solarsystemid/shipid), beyonce binding is released and SCT recorded. Test: kill victim with a second session attached, assert notifications and that immediate Dock returns SessionChangeInProgress.
rows.title: Ship/pod death pushes session change and starts SCT

rows.acceptance: record_session_change_timer is called on character login, CloneJump, and jump drive/bridge/portal arrival; jump-drive arrival grants the 60s location-change invulnerability. Tests per handler.
rows.title: SCT on login, clone jump and jump drive; jump-drive arrival invulnerability

rows.acceptance: RemoveBall (dock, jump, logoff removal, death) removes all ActiveModuleCycle entries for that ship, clears snap.module_active_states for its modules and emits deactivation; no cycle survives for a ship not in the ballpark. Test: activate a repeater, dock, assert no active cycle remains in the old system actor.
rows.title: Module cycles cleared when a ship leaves a ballpark

rows.acceptance: A started self-destruct detonates at T+120s via a lazily-checked or ticked server timer even if the client disconnects or never calls again; countdown persisted across restart. Test: start, disconnect session, advance clock 121s, assert ship destroyed and killmail created.
rows.title: Self-destruct completes server-side

rows.acceptance: Inline weapon death path creates the wreck with owner_id=victim character and leaves dropped items owned by the victim; looting by others follows theft rules. Test: kill player, assert wreck.owner_id==victim.
rows.title: Wreck and dropped loot owned by the victim

rows.acceptance: execute_death_pipeline for a capsule spawns a corpse item/ball (no 26557 wreck) and lists active implants as destroyed on the killmail, matching the inline weapon path.
rows.title: Canonical death pipeline: pod leaves corpse, no wreck

rows.acceptance: Every space container item (wreck incl. 26557, cargo container 23, corpse 25, dropped loot) stores its position in item_positions when spawned. On system actor spawn, a ball is re-created for every item with location_id == system and a stored position. Lifetimes are persisted (created_unix on the item), not kept in the static COMBAT_RUNTIME. Test: kill ship -> restart repository/actors -> wreck ball present at same position with same contents and despawns at created+7200s.
rows.title: Wrecks, jetcans and corpses survive server restart

rows.acceptance: When daily downtime runs, all NPC-kill wrecks and their contents are deleted from items and from the ballpark. Test: spawn NPC wreck, run downtime, wreck gone.
rows.title: NPC wrecks removed at daily downtime

rows.acceptance: invbroker.Add/MultiAdd from a wreck (any flag) or jetcan owned by another character, not same player corp or fleet and not abandoned, sets a 900s suspect flag and broadcasts OnSuspectsAndCriminalsUpdate. Safety Green rejects it with no state change. Same corp/fleet/abandoned is free.
rows.title: Per-item theft from wrecks/cans follows loot rules

rows.acceptance: beyonce.CmdAbandonLoot(wreckIDs) by the owner marks the wrecks/cans abandoned, persistently and visibly via slim item. Afterwards anyone can loot via LootAll/Add without a suspect flag. A non-owner call is rejected.
rows.title: Abandon wreck/can (beyonce.CmdAbandonLoot)

rows.acceptance: A successful salvage of a wreck that still contains items creates a cargo container (type 23, owner = wreck owner) at the wreck position, moves all contents into it, and spawns its ball. If contents exceed the container capacity, salvage fails with SalvageTooMuchLootBody and nothing changes. Items are never orphaned.
rows.title: Salvaging a wreck with loot spills it into a cargo container

rows.acceptance: When the last item leaves a jettison container (type 23 in space), the container item and its ball are removed and the ball removal is broadcast to the system.
rows.title: Empty jetcan despawns

rows.acceptance: posMgr.AnchorStructure dispatches by group: anchorable secure/audit containers anchor as plain containers with no warp bubble. Only group 361 (mobile warp disruptor) creates a bubble. Anchored containers persist their position and despawn 30 days after deployment.
rows.title: Anchoring secure containers (not warp bubbles)

rows.acceptance: Anchor completion is computed from the persisted anchor_start_unix (works with no subscribers). The bubble is re-created on actor spawn after a restart. The disruptor is removed 2 days after anchoring.
rows.title: Mobile warp disruptor: wall-clock anchoring, 2-day decay, restart persistence

rows.acceptance: On system actor spawn, every structure with solar_system_id == system and state != Destroyed gets its ball (ensure_structure_ball_in_space). Test: anchor -> restart -> ball present and targetable; AttackStructure and docking work.
rows.title: Upwell structure balls are re-created after restart

rows.acceptance: When a structure is destroyed or its unanchor completes during the lazy sync, its ball is removed and OnStructureRemoved is sent at completion, not at unanchor start. The dropped quantum core, fittings and the packaged structure item each get a ball at the structure position.
rows.title: Destroyed/unanchored structures leave grid; drops are visible

rows.acceptance: If power_state == Abandoned when destroyed, hangar contents are not wrapped into asset safety; they drop or are destroyed as loot at the structure position. Non-abandoned K-space structures keep asset safety.
rows.title: Abandoned structure destruction drops items instead of asset safety

rows.acceptance: Wraps not delivered within 20 days are moved lazily, on any read of wraps or assets, to the nearest NPC station by AU in the allowed security band (null->low, low->low, high->high). Manual delivery after 5 days to a station or structure in the same system costs 0.5% of value. Retrieving from an auto-delivered wrap costs 15%.
rows.title: Asset safety 20-day auto-delivery and fee tiers

rows.acceptance: An order with issue+duration<=now is never returned by GetOrders/GetRegionBest/GetStationAsks/GetCharOrders/GetCorporationOrders and never matched by PlaceBuyOrder/PlaceMultiSellOrder/BuyMultipleItems; first touch after expiry (any path, or owner login) returns sell items to the order station hangar and refunds buy escrow exactly once; OnMarketItemReceived carries the order's stationID.
rows.title: Market order expiry enforced on every read/match path

rows.acceptance: With production sqlite world DB: place an order (duration 1), install a corp job, build a PI network; restart server; order keeps issue date/duration/range/account key and expires on schedule, corp job delivers to corp, PI pins/links/routes/programs intact.
rows.title: owner_notes (order meta, job meta, PI networks) survive restart

rows.acceptance: Extractor stops producing at install+duration; decay curve keyed to time since install; leftover partial cycle carried; repeated GetColony/StartTicking calls cannot increase total yield vs a single call at the same end time; output beyond storage capacity is lost; extractor-finished/storage-full notifications persisted for offline owner.
rows.title: PI extractor programs expire and offline sim is time-accurate

rows.acceptance: UserLaunchCommodities never places goods in a station hangar; it creates a launch canister in space at the planet visible in Planetary Launches; uncollected after 5 days it is removed; DeleteLaunch only accepts launch ids.
rows.title: Command-center launch creates orbit canister with 5-day lifetime

rows.acceptance: DeleteCharacter: cancels market orders (items/escrow follow asset rule), removes outstanding contracts, resolves jobs/colonies, transfers wallet ISK to player corp division 1 as Inheritance (NPC corp: destroyed) and assets to corp hangar, mails corp members; refused while CEO.
rows.title: Biomass resolves orders, contracts, jobs, colonies and ISK

rows.acceptance: for_corp contract reward/fees debit corp wallet division; price/refunds/collateral credit corp wallet; issuer leaving corp does not redirect proceeds; requires corp contract roles.
rows.title: Corp contracts use corp wallet and stay with corp

rows.acceptance: Destroying a ship carrying a courier wrap rolls/destroys the wrap contents (no orphan items with dangling location); contract becomes Failed with collateral to issuer; deadline failure never teleports items regardless of collateral.
rows.title: Courier package destruction and failure keep items consistent

rows.acceptance: CompleteManyJobs delivers every listed ready job; jobs whose end time precedes facility offline are not paused; pause starts at the offline moment, not first read; ex-members cannot cancel/deliver corp jobs.
rows.title: Industry pause timing and CompleteManyJobs

rows.acceptance: With a training queue and an Omega expiry at T in the past: on next login the server credits training at Omega rate only up to T. It then sets clone_grade=1 and pauses the queue (no SP accrues after T, and over-cap entries are neither skipped nor reordered). The queue resumes at Alpha rate only after an explicit resume. Test: queue with an above-cap skill at the head plus an Alpha skill behind it, expiry mid-way; assert SP == omega_rate*(T-start) and the second skill gained no SP.
rows.title: Skill queue on Omega lapse

rows.acceptance: charMgr.AddContact, BlockOwners and contact labels are stored in the world DB. After a server restart GetContacts returns the same contacts, standings, watchlist flags, blocks and labels; mail from a blocked sender is still refused, and the CSPA friendly-contact exemption still applies.
rows.title: Personal contacts/blocks/labels persisted

rows.acceptance: authentication.Logout of a fleet member removes them from fleet.members, member_details, wing/squad commander slots and the fleet channel, and sends OnFleetLeave to the remaining members. If they were boss, boss passes (OnFleetMemberChanged with the fleetJobCreator bit); if no members remain the fleet and its channel are deleted.
rows.title: Fleet member logout leaves fleet

rows.acceptance: On socket disconnect the member stays in the fleet for a bounded grace period. Relogging within it restores session.fleet_id (fleetObjectHandler.Reconnect rejoins the same position); after it expires, the logout removal runs (OnFleetLeave, boss pass, empty-fleet disband). Works for the boss too.
rows.title: Fleet membership grace period on disconnect

rows.acceptance: After relogging, GetFleetID, session.fleet_id and snap.fleets agree. A character listed in a fleet either gets session.fleet_id restored or is removed. AcceptInvite, ApplyToJoin and CreateFleet refuse a character already in another fleet, so no character is ever in two fleets.
rows.title: Single consistent fleet membership after relogin

rows.acceptance: After a server restart (or downtime) no fleet with offline members is reloaded. Either fleets are dropped at startup, or all fleet state (fleet_extras names, max size, invites, adverts, fleet channel) is restored consistently and offline members are removed per the disconnect rule.
rows.title: Fleets do not resurrect with ghost members after restart

rows.acceptance: KickMember/ForceLeaveFleet on an online target pushes a session change clearing the target's fleetid. Every fleet RPC (Invite, MoveMember, broadcasts, etc.) checks that the caller is in fleet.member_details and has the required role; a kicked member's Invite fails.
rows.title: Kicked fleet member loses fleet session

rows.acceptance: Inviting an offline character, one already in a fleet, or one with another pending invite fails with the matching user error. Pending invites expire (and are not persisted across restart).
rows.title: Fleet invites require online, fleetless target and expire

rows.acceptance: PrepareCharacterForDelete fails for a corp CEO. DeleteCharacter removes the character from corp.members/member_roles and from any fleet, and cancels their market orders and outstanding contracts. Player-corp member: all assets incl. capsule move to the corp's first hangar division (destroyed if no office), wallet ISK goes to corp wallet division 1 with an 'Inheritance' journal entry, and every corp member receives an EVE mail. NPC-corp member: assets and ISK are destroyed.
rows.title: Biomass side effects

rows.acceptance: KickOutMember on an online target pushes a session change (corpid to NPC corp, corprole=0, allianceid=None) to the target's session. Afterwards the target's corp hangar, wallet and bookmark-ACL calls fail, and the target is removed from the corpid: channel.
rows.title: Expelled online member loses corp session immediately

rows.acceptance: Expelling a member with roles or role-granting titles fails until the roles are dropped and 24h have passed since the drop (persisted timestamp). An undocked member goes on a persisted Auto Removal list and is removed when they next dock, or at downtime. Quitting to an NPC corp is always allowed (except for the CEO).
rows.title: Corp expel rules: roles, 24h timer, auto-removal on dock/downtime

rows.acceptance: Titles and member titles, the role audit log, pending role grants, medals and recipients, bulletins, recruitment ads, corp contacts and labels, welcome mail, friendly-fire settings and employment history (CORP_GOV, EMP_HISTORY) are stored in the world DB. After a restart AuditMember, GetEmploymentRecord, titles and their granted roles, and pending 24h hangar grants are unchanged.
rows.title: Corp governance state persisted (D-6)

rows.acceptance: Accepting an application or invitation removes the character from the old corp's members and member_roles. It is refused if the character holds roles in the old corp (or dropped them under 24h ago), is CEO of the old corp, or is not docked. An online applicant gets a session change.
rows.title: Joining a corp removes old membership and enforces join rules

rows.acceptance: corpRegistry.InsertInvitation never adds the target to the corp, whatever the arguments. Membership changes only when the target accepts while online and eligible. Test: inviter passes accept_now=True for an offline target; assert the target's corporation_id is unchanged.
rows.title: Corp invitations require target acceptance

rows.acceptance: Self-quit moves the character to the default NPC corp for their bloodline/school (not a hard-coded ID). It clears member_titles, pending role grants and account keys for that corp, removes them from the corpid: channel and adds them to the NPC corp channel.
rows.title: Quitting corp: bloodline NPC corp and full cleanup

rows.acceptance: SendMail to an offline character succeeds no matter how many mails exist server-wide; only per-character mailbox limits apply. Test: 3,001 mails across many recipients; mail number 3,002 is delivered and appears in the offline recipient's SyncMail at next login.
rows.title: No server-wide mail cap blocks delivery

rows.acceptance: read_mails, deleted_mails, mail_assigned_labels, trashed mails, mailing lists (members, operators, settings, welcome mail) and calendar events are stored in the world DB. After a restart, unread counts, labels (Sent/Corp/Alliance/custom), trash contents and deletions are unchanged, and mailing-list membership survives.
rows.title: Mail read/labels/trash/deleted and mailing lists persisted

rows.acceptance: Bookmarks keep folder_id, subfolder, memo/note, item_id, is_shared and expiry across restart, and bookmark_folders (with ACLs) persist. A bookmark created with a 3h expiry is still deleted at its expiry when that falls after a restart.
rows.title: Bookmark fields, folders and expiry persisted

rows.acceptance: On authentication.Logout and on socket disconnect the character is removed from the solarsystemid2 channel (and other joined channels) and OnChannelLeft (or equivalent) goes to channel members, so Local's member list no longer shows them.
rows.title: Logged-off characters leave Local and other channels

rows.acceptance: Player-owned channels (name, owner, operators, password, allow/deny lists, bans/mutes, MOTD) survive a server restart, and members can rejoin them.
rows.title: Player-owned chat channels persisted
